Stir in flour, curry powder, and cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any brown bits at the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer. Then add carrots, spinach, potatoes, and turkey.
Bring to a boil. Then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer (covered) for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve in bowls and garnish with a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
Heat oil in a large sauté pan.
Sauté onion over medium heat, until light brown, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Add sliced cabbage, salt, black pepper, and caraway seeds.
Stir and cook for 30 minutes.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Savory and Spicy Ground Beef & Succotash

steps.text: Brown ground beef in pan. Drain excess liquid.
Add remaining ingredients except nutmeg. Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Sprinkle with nutmeg before serving.
Cook rice according to directions on the package.
Combine the cooked rice, bouillon granules, and scallions and mix well.
Measure 1-cup portions and serve.
Wash potatoes; peel and slice into thin slices.
Melt 1 tablespoon of margarine in heavy, deep skillet. Remove skillet from heat; spread half of potato slices in skillet.
Cover potatoes with onions. Sprinkle half of flour and pepper over potato mixture.
Add remaining potato slices, flour, and pepper. Cut 1 tablespoon of margarine into small pieces and place on top of potato mixture.
Pour milk over potato mixture; bring to boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium low, cover, and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix chicken, vegetable oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
If using taco seasoning or chili powder, add that too.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap, and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
While the chicken is in the refrigerator, cook the pepper and onion on a stovetop over medium heat until done (about 12 minutes).
Cook the chicken over medium heat. Cook each side about 10 to 15 minutes.
Place chicken on a plate. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Cut the chicken into strips.
To make the tacos, put chicken on the tortilla first. Add peppers and onion strips next. Top with lettuce, tomato, and salsa. If using parsley or cilantro, add that too.
Mix 3 1/2 cups of the milk with the pudding mixes. Beat the pudding mixture with a wire whisk for 2 minutes until it is well blended. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Fold 1 cup of the whipped topping into the pudding mix.

Arrange a layer of wafers on the bottom and sides of a 2-quart serving bowl. Drizzle 2 tablespoons of the remaining milk over the wafers. Add a layer of banana slices and top with one-third of the pudding.
Repeat layers, drizzling each wafer layer with remaining milk and ending with pudding. Spread the remaining whipped topping over the pudding.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours before serving.
Preheat the oven to 400 °F.
Put the potatoes in a non-stick skillet on the stove and cover with cold water. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook about 15 minutes until the potatoes are easily pierced with a knife.
Drain the potatoes well and set aside to cool. Then peel and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Put the eggs, salt, and pepper in the bowl and mix well with a whisk.
Return the skillet on the stove and turn the heat to medium-high. Add the oil. Add onion and cook about 5 minutes until soft. Add the cubed potatoes.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes and onions. Press down with a spatula to make an even layer and shake gently to prevent sticking. Lower to medium heat and cook about 7 minutes.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and cook until the frittata is completely set, about 5 minutes.
Gently loosen frittata from the pan. Place a serving plate over the skillet and carefully invert the frittata onto the plate.
Slice into 4 wedges. Serve warm.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Cook potatoes in boiling water until tender.
In a nonstick pan, add oil or vegetable spray and warm at medium heat.
Add the onion and sauté until brown. Add vegetables and sauté until tender but not brown.
In a medium mixing bowl, slightly beat the eggs and egg whites, pepper, garlic salt, and mozzarella cheese. Stir egg cheese mixture into the cooked vegetables.
Oil or spray a 10-inch pie pan or ovenproof skillet. Transfer potatoes and eggs mixture to pan. Spread with parmesan cheese and bake omelet until firm and brown on top, about 20 to 30 minutes.
Put chicken, hot sauce, mustard, thyme, and garlic in the bowl and mix well. Cover and refrigerate at least one hour or up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 450 °F.
Put the chicken on a baking sheet and sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Place in the oven and bake about 50 minutes until crispy and crackling. Serve right away.
Combine all ingredients except chicken in saucepan.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Place chicken on large platter and brush with half the sauce mixture.
Cover with plastic wrap and marinate in refrigerator for 1 hour.
Remove plastic wrap from chicken. Place chicken on baking sheet lined with aluminum foil and broil for 10 minutes on each side to seal in juices.
Remove from broiler and add remaining sauce to chicken. Cover with aluminum foil and bake at 350 °F for 30 minutes.
Place all ingredients in a large saucepan. Cover.
Heat thoroughly over medium-high heat, about 10 minutes. Add seasonings to taste.
Put soup pot on the stove on medium heat. Add oil when the pot is hot.
Add onion, carrots, celery, and thyme and cook 10 to 15 minutes, until tender.
Add split peas, stock, and 4 cups water. Raise the heat to high and bring to a boil.

Lower the heat to low and cook about 2 hours, partially covered, until the peas have fallen apart. Check the soup during cooking. If more water is needed, add up to 2 cups. Skim off any foam that forms.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to three days. Stir in the lemon juice just before serving.
Mix the wheat and barley nugget cereal, bran cereal, sunflower seeds, and almonds in a medium bowl.
Add the raisins, the bananas, and half of the strawberries.
Gently stir in the yogurt and divide between two bowls.
Scatter the remaining strawberries over the top and enjoy!

Combine first 10 ingredients in large saucepan. Cook for 10 minutes (up to black pepper), then stir in tomato paste. Cover and cook gently, 15 minutes, stirring occasionally until vegetables are tender.
Cook spaghetti in unsalted water according to package directions.
Spoon sauce over drained hot spaghetti and sprinkle Parmesan cheese over top.
Heat oil in medium saucepan. Add celery and onions and saute until tender, about 10 minutes.
Add water, orange and lemon juice, and hot sauce. Bring to a boil. Stir in rice and bring back to a boil. Let stand covered until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Stir in almonds. Serve immediately as a side dish for a fish entree.
In a medium bowl, flake tuna with fork. Stir in beans, corn, mayonnaise, taco seasoning*, and lime juice.
Place lettuce, cheese, and salsa in separate bowls.
Place tortillas or taco shells on microwave safe plate. Microwave on high for 1 minute.**
To eat, layer tuna mixture, lettuce, and cheese on tortilla. Top with salsa.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a small bowl, combine milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, and oatmeal. Mix well and set aside.
In a medium-sized baking pan, add the sweet potatoes so that they cover the bottom of the pan.
Add the oatmeal mixture on top of the sweet potatoes.
Bake for 20 minutes. Serve hot or refrigerate and serve cold.
In a medium bowl, stir together sweet potato and banana.
Add milk, blending well.
Add brown sugar, egg yolks, and salt, mixing thoroughly.
Spray casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray. Transfer sweet potato mixture to casserole dish.
Bake in preheated 325 °F oven for 35 minutes. Remove from oven.
Combine raisins, sugar, and cinnamon; sprinkle over top of sweet potato mixture.
Return to oven and bake 10 more minutes.
Put sweet potatoes and water in a skillet and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the water has been absorbed by the sweet potatoes.

Add oil, sausage, onion, bell pepper and garlic to the skillet with the sweet potatoes. Cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onion is lightly browned and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Divide the hash between 4 plates and return the skillet to the stove.
Reheat the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the remaining 1 teaspoon oil.
Add the eggs, one at a time, and cook about 3 to 5 minutes until the whites are solid and the yolks begin to thicken but are not hard. Flip the egg and cook for one more minute.
Top sweet potato hash with an egg and serve right away.
Combine all ingredients and stir just until large lumps disappear. Note: Over-stirring will result in tough pancakes.
Pour slightly less than 1/4 cup batter for each pancake onto skillet or electric griddle heated to 350 to 375 °F.
When pancakes bubble around edges and towards center, sprinkle with chopped nuts (if you choose). Then, flip pancakes.
Pancake is done when bottoms are golden brown.
Serve with applesauce or syrup.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to create a crease. Unfold.
Place each chicken breast in the middle of the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper (if desired).
Top chicken with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 165 °F, about 20 minutes, depending the thickness of the chicken breast.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Cut four large rectangles of parchment paper or aluminum foil and fold in half to crease. Unfold.
Put each fish fillet on the foil or parchment paper and season with salt and pepper.
Top fish with your choice of vegetables and seasonings.
Drizzle each packet with 1/2 teaspoon oil and 1 teaspoon lemon juice.
Fold the parchment paper or foil in half and then crimp around the edges tightly in 1/4-inch folds to create a half moon shape.
Using a spatula, transfer the packets to a baking sheet. Bake until the fish is cooked to an internal temperature of 145 °F, about 10 to 12 minutes, depending the thickness of the fish.
In a medium saucepan, cook onion in oil over medium heat, stirring frequently until golden brown, about 4 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute longer. Add chopped tomatoes.
Cook uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spoon 3/4 of mixture into food processor or blender container; puree until smooth. Return to saucepan.
Add red pepper, basil, and reconstitute milk to the soup. Heat until hot, but do not boil. Season to taste with salt and pepper (optional). Serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Bake in 9x5 loaf pan for 25 minutes or until it reaches an internal temperature of 165 °F. Check the temperature with a meat thermometer.
Cut into five slices and serve.
Rinse and core cabbage. Carefully remove 10 outer leaves, place in saucepan, and cover with boiling water. Simmer 5 minutes. Remove and drain cooked cabbage leaves on paper towels.
Shred 1/2 cup of raw cabbage and set aside.
Brown ground beef and turkey and minced onion in skillet. Drain fat.
Place cooked and drained meat mixture, bread crumbs, water, and pepper into mixing bowl.

Drain tomatoes, reserving liquid, and add 1/2 cup of tomato juice from can to meat mixture. Mix well; then place 1/4 cup of filling on each parboiled, drained cabbage leaf. Place folded side down in large skillet.
In skillet top cabbages with tomatoes, sliced onion, water, shredded cabbage, and carrot. Cover and simmer about 1 hour (or until cabbage is tender), basting occasionally.
Remove cabbage rolls to serving platter; keep warm.
Mix lemon juice, brown sugar, and cornstarch together in small bowl. Add to vegetables and liquid in skillet, and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened and clear. Serve over cabbage rolls.
Put the pot over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onions, zucchini, sweet potatoes, garlic, and spices and cook, stirring from time to time, for 20 minutes.
Add the kidney beans and tomatoes. Stir and cook, covered, until the squash is tender, about 30 minutes.
Add the corn and cook until warmed throughout.
Serve right away or transfer to a container once cooled. Refrigerate up to 5 days.
To cook the pasta, fill a pot halfway with water. Bring it to a boil over high heat. When it has boiled, add the pasta and cook until just tender, about 12 minutes. Drain the pasta and set aside.

While the pasta is cooking, cook the stroganoff: Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil. Add the onion, garlic, carrots, zucchini, peppers, and dried basil and cook until soft and golden, about 20 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the sauce comes together, about 20 minutes.
Put the yogurt and tomato paste in the bowl, stirring until smooth.

Turn the heat off and move the vegetables in the skillet to one side. Gradually add the tomato paste mixture to the other side of the skillet, stirring all the while. Turn the heat to low and cook about 5 minutes, until heated through.
Add the cooked pasta and stir until mixed.
In a medium skillet, heat oil. Cook onions, garlic, and zucchini in oil for 5 minutes on medium heat.
Add remaining ingredients and simmer covered for 45 minutes. Serve over pasta.
In a large bowl, combine corn and cornmeal.
Add onions, green pepper, rice, chili powder, and pepper. If using cayenne and jalapeño chilies, add them too. Mix well.
Form the burger mixture into 6 equal patties about 1/2 inch thick, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Spray both sides of the patties with nonstick cooking spray.
In a large pan, brown both sides of the patties over medium to high heat for 5 to 8 minutes.
Bake the patties in the oven for 10 minutes.
Toast the flour tortillas in the oven for 8 minutes.
Place patty on half of tortilla and fold tortilla over to serve like a taco.
Boil water in a cooking pot. Add the pasta. Turn down the heat to medium-low; cook according to box directions. Pour pasta and water into colander to drain.
Add vegetables and spaghetti sauce to cooking pot. Cook over medium-low heat just until the vegetables are hot.
Return cooked, drained pasta back to cooking pot and mix together.
Sprinkle with cheese just before serving.
Mix all ingredients together.
Serve.
Prick potatoes with fork. Bake at 425 °F for 60 minutes or until fork is easily inserted.
Cut potatoes in half lengthwise. Carefully scoop out potato, leaving about 1/2 inch of pulp inside shell. Mash pulp in large bowl.
Mix in by hand remaining ingredients except Parmesan cheese. Spoon mixture into potato shells.
Sprinkle top with 1/4 teaspoon of Parmesan cheese.
Place on baking sheet and return to oven. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown.
Line up 4 parfait or other tall glasses.
Spoon 1/2 cup of yogurt into each glass.
Sprinkle with granola.
Top with about 1/4 cup of fruit.
Spray sauté pan with cooking spray. Preheat over high heat.
Cook chicken in hot sauté pan, stirring for 3–5 minutes. Reduce heat.
Add tomatoes with juice, chili sauce, green pepper, celery, onion, garlic, basil, parsley, crushed red pepper, and salt. Bring to boil over high heat, and then reduce heat to simmer.
Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.
Bake fresh, unsalted salmon (until it flakes easily with a fork in the thickest part). Flake, place in a bowl, and chill.
After salmon has chilled, stir in the remaining ingredients.
Season with black pepper to taste.
Serve as a side dish or salad, or spread on pilot bread or unsalted crackers.

Combine chicken broth, mushroom caps, ginger, scallions, soy sauce, and sesame oil (optional) in a large, shallow sauté pan. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower heat and simmer for 2–3 minutes.

Add salmon fillets, and cover with a tight-fitting lid. Cook gently over low heat for 4–5 minutes or until the salmon flakes easily with a fork in the thickest part (to a minimum internal temperature of 145 °F).
Serve one piece of salmon with ¼ cup of broth.

Place 1 inch of water in a 4-quart pot with a lid. Place a steamer basket inside the pot, and add asparagus. Cover and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for 5–10 minutes, until asparagus is easily pierced with a sharp knife. Do not overcook.

While the asparagus cooks, grate the lemon zest into a small bowl. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze the juice into the bowl. Use the back of a spoon to press out extra juice and remove pits. Add mayonnaise, parsley, pepper, and salt. Stir well. Set aside.
When the asparagus is tender, remove the pot from the heat. Place asparagus spears in a serving bowl. Drizzle the lemon sauce evenly over the asparagus (about 1½ teaspoons per portion) and serve.
Sprinkle lemon juice on the apple slices.
Mix the lettuce, cranberries, apple, walnuts, and sunflower seeds in a bowl.
Toss with raspberry vinaigrette dressing, to lightly cover the salad, and serve.

recipes.title: Baby Spinach With Golden Raisins and Pine Nuts

steps.text: In a medium nonstick pan over high heat, cook and stir the pine nuts until they begin to brown lightly and smell toasted, but not burnt. Set the pine nuts aside in another dish.

Return the pan to the burner over medium-high heat. Add ¼ cup water. As it begins to boil, add a small handful of the spinach. Cook and stir just until it begins to wilt. Then push it to the side of the pan, and add another ¼ cup water and handful of spinach. Continue until all the spinach has been cooked, adding the raisins with the last handful of spinach.
Sprinkle with nutmeg and salt. Cook and stir until all the spinach is wilted and the raisins are warm.
Remove from heat. Press out excess water. Place 1 cup spinach and raisins in a serving bowl. Top with pine nuts.
Preheat oven to 475 °F.
Drizzle lemon juice on fish. Then, pat dry.
Combine milk, hot sauce, and garlic in a mixing bowl.
Combine white pepper, salt, and onion powder with cornflakes, and spread on a plate.
Let fillets sit briefly in milk mixture. Remove a fillet, coat on both sides with seasoned crumbs, and let stand briefly until coating sticks to each side of fish. Repeat for all fillets.
Arrange fillets on a lightly oiled shallow baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes on middle rack without turning.
Cut into 6 pieces. Serve with fresh lemon.
Scrub potatoes and cut them into long ½-inch strips. Place the strips in the ice water, cover, and chill for 1 hour or longer.
Remove potato strips and dry them thoroughly. Preheat oven to 475 °F.
Place garlic powder, onion powder, salt, white pepper, allspice, and pepper flakes in a plastic bag. Toss the potato strips in the spice mixture.
Put the potato strips in a shallow baking pan, and brush them with oil.
Cover the baking pan with aluminum foil, and bake at 475 °F for 15 minutes.
Remove the foil, and continue baking, uncovered, for an additional 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown. Turn fries occasionally to brown on all sides.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Whisk sour cream, dill, scallions, mustard, and lemon juice in a small bowl to blend.
Lightly coat baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place salmon, skin side down, on the prepared baking sheet. Sprinkle with garlic powder and pepper, then spread with sauce.
Bake salmon fillets until each is opaque in the center and flakes easily with a fork in the thickest part, about 20 minutes (to a minimum internal temperature of 145 °F).
Serve immediately.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Spray baking dish with cooking spray.
Arrange fillets in the baking dish. The dish should be large enough so the fillets do not overlap.
Mix remaining ingredients, except parsley and lemon wedges, in a bowl.
Spoon the tomato mixture evenly over the fillets.
Bake uncovered 15 to 20 minutes or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Garnish with parsley and a lemon wedge, and serve.
Heat butter in a large sauté pan. Add leeks and carrots, and cook gently for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add potatoes, chicken broth, parsley, and salt and pepper, and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat and simmer gently until the vegetables are just tender, about 10–12 minutes.

Add cod fillets, and cover with a tight-fitting lid. Continue cooking over low heat for an additional 5 minutes or until the fish is white and flakes easily with a fork in the thickest part (to a minimum internal temperature of 145 °F).
Serve each cod fillet with 1½ cups broth and vegetables.
Preheat oven to 350 ºF.
Heat olive oil in a medium-sized heavy-bottom roasting or braising pan (a large sauté pan with a metal handle will work as well).

Add mushrooms to pan, and cook until golden brown, about 3–5 minutes. Add leeks, potatoes, celery, and pearl onions, and continue to cook until the vegetables become soft, about 3–5 additional minutes.

Add chicken broth to the pan, and bring to a boil. Add chicken legs to the pan, cover, and place in the heated oven for about 20 minutes or until the chicken legs are tender when pierced with a fork (to a minimum internal temperature of 165 °F).
When chicken legs are tender, remove legs from the pan, return the pan to the stovetop, and bring the liquid to a boil. Add herbs and lemon juice.
In a bowl, mix the cornstarch with the sour cream, and add to the pan. Bring back to a boil and then remove from the heat.
Season with salt and pepper, and pour 1 cup of vegetables and sauce over chicken.
Spray a heavy iron skillet with cooking spray, and preheat over medium heat. Brown the chicken cubes, in batches, with cooking spray as needed.
Place the meat in a 3- or 4-quart casserole (with cover), and add the remaining ingredients.
Deglaze the skillet: On high heat, add some cold water and scrape the hardened juices with a spoon or spatula to dissolve them into the water. Add the sauce to the casserole.
Add water to barely cover the ingredients. Cover the casserole, and simmer until the stew is thick and the meat is very tender, about 1½ hours.
Add black pepper to taste before serving.
Heat olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell peppers, and garlic, and sauté until vegetables are soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, and stir fry for another 5–10 minutes until chicken is no longer pink inside.
Add the tomato sauce, chicken broth, lemon juice, cumin, bay leaves, water, and raisins to the vegetables and chicken.
Cover the pan, and reduce the heat. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, and garnish with fresh cilantro, capers, and green olives, and serve.
Bake chicken, cut into cubes, and refrigerate.
In a large bowl, combine the rest of the ingredients. Add chilled chicken, and mix well.

recipes.title: Cold Fusilli Pasta with Summer Vegetables

steps.text: In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.
Add pasta, and cook according to package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 8–9 minutes. Drain. Rinse pasta under cold running water to cool, about 3 minutes.
Place all the vegetables and beans in a large salad serving bowl. Season with basil, salt, and pepper.
Add the cooled pasta.
Combine olive oil and vinegar in a small bowl. Mix until completely blended. Pour over vegetables and pasta. Mix gently until well coated.
Divide into four equal portions. Top each with 2 tablespoons shredded parmesan cheese.

recipes.title: Couscous With Carrots, Walnuts, and Raisins

steps.text: In a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat, cook and stir couscous, olive oil, walnuts, salt, pepper, and spice just until couscous begins to brown.
Slowly add water, then raisins and carrots. Cover. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Remove from the heat, and let stand for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Creamy Squash Soup With Shredded Apples

steps.text: Place the frozen squash in a microwave-safe dish. Cover loosely. Defrost in the microwave on medium power for 5–10 minutes, until mostly thawed.
Meanwhile, peel then shred the apples using a grater or food processor, or peel and finely chop apples into thin strips. Set aside ¼ cup.
Warm oil in a 4-quart saucepan over medium heat. Add all but ¼ cup of the apples. Cook and stir until apples soften, about 5 minutes.
Stir in thawed squash and pumpkin pie spice.
Add the evaporated milk about ½ cup at a time, stirring after each addition.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook and stir over high heat just until soup is about to boil.
Ladle into individual soup bowls. Top each with a tablespoon of the unused apples. Sprinkle with additional pumpkin pie spice, if desired.
Rinse green beans and snap off tips.
Place green beans in a large pot and add ½ cup of cold water.
Cook green beans on stovetop over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Spray a sauté pan with cooking spray, and sauté the chopped onions and garlic for 5 minutes, or until they are tender and very lightly browned.

Add onions, garlic, and black pepper to green beans. Spray the cooking spray over mixture, and cook on medium heat for another 20 minutes or until green beans are tender, but not soft. Stir occasionally.
Sprinkle dried basil and oregano over green beans. Mix and serve.
Prepare the filling: Heat oil in a sauté pan, and sauté the ground meat with the shrimp and garlic.
Add the vegetables (cabbage, green beans, carrots, celery, and jicama), and sauté until slightly crisp.
Add the chicken broth, and continue until vegetables are cooked. Season with salt and black pepper.
Remove from heat and use a colander to strain; save the broth for use in preparing the lumpia sauce (steps below). Let meat and vegetable mixture cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, prepare the sauce: Mix 1 cup of the broth strained from the cooked filling, soy sauce, brown sugar, and garlic together in a saucepan, and bring to a boil.
In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch in 2 tablespoons of cold water. Slowly add the cornstarch mixture to the broth in the saucepan. Stir over medium heat until sauce thickens.
To assemble the spring rolls: Soak one spring roll wrapper in warm water until soft and transparent. Dry immediately with a paper towel.
Place the wrapper on a plate, and lay a piece of lettuce on the wrapper. Put 2 tablespoons of the meat and vegetable mixture on the wrapper.
Fold bottom of wrapper over filling; wrap one side over filling and roll to the other side (to seal in the filling).
Repeat with remaining wrappers and filling.
Serve with lumpia sauce on top. Sprinkle with chopped peanuts.
In a large bowl, place potatoes, celery, green onion, and parsley.
Meanwhile, in a blender or food processor, blend cottage cheese, milk, lemon juice, vinegar, celery seed, dill weed, dry mustard, and white pepper until smooth. Chill for 1 hour.
Pour chilled cottage cheese mixture over vegetables; mix well.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Thread six grapes, alternating grape colors, onto each wooden skewer.
Place skewers into the freezer for 30 minutes, or until frozen.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Grilled Tuna With Chickpea and Spinach Salad

steps.text: Preheat grill pan or oven broiler (with the rack 3 inches from heat source) on high temperature.
Combine oil, garlic, lemon juice, and oregano, and brush over tuna steaks. Marinate for 5–10 minutes.
Meanwhile, combine all salad ingredients. (Salad can be made up to 2 hours in advance and refrigerated.)
Grill or broil tuna on high heat for 3–4 minutes on each side until the flesh is opaque and separates easily with a fork (to a minimum internal temperature of 145 °F).
Serve one tuna steak over 1 cup of mixed salad.
Preheat a broiler or grill on medium-high heat.
Thread three chicken cubes and three pineapple chunks alternately on each skewer.
Combine ingredients for sauce and mix well; separate into two bowls and set one aside for later.
Grill skewers for 3–5 minutes on each side. Brush or spoon sauce (from the bowl that wasn’t set aside) onto chicken and pineapple about every other minute. Discard the sauce when done with this step.

To prevent chicken from drying out, finish cooking skewers in a 350 °F oven immediately after grilling (to a minimum internal temperature of 165 °F). Using a clean brush or spoon, coat with sauce from the set-aside bowl before serving.

recipes.title: Heavenly Chicken With Angel Hair Pasta

steps.text: In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.
While the water heats, chop onion, mince garlic, and cut broccoli into tiny florets. Set aside.
In a large nonstick pan, heat olive oil until very hot. Add the chicken. Cook and stir until lightly browned on both sides, about 5–8 minutes. Place chicken on a clean plate, and cover to keep warm.
Coat pan with cooking spray. Over medium heat, cook and stir the onion for about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and broccoli. Cook and stir for 2 more minutes.

Return the chicken to the pan. Add entire jar of pasta sauce, cayenne pepper, and salt. Gently mix to blend ingredients. Cover. Simmer until chicken and vegetables are warmed through, about 4 minutes.
Drop pasta into boiling water. Cook according to package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 2 minutes. Drain.
Divide pasta among four dinner plates (about 1 cup each). Top each with one-fourth of the chicken and sauce mixture. Serve immediately.
Place turkey carcass in a large 6-quart pot. Cover with water, at least ¾ full.
Peel onions, cut into large pieces, and add to pot. Wash celery stalks, slice, and add to pot as well.
Simmer, covered, for about 2 ½ hours.
Remove carcass from pot. Cool soup in the refrigerator (hint: divide soup into smaller, shallower containers for quicker cooling).
While soup is cooling, remove remaining meat from turkey carcass. Discard bones and cut meat into bite-sized pieces.
After soup has cooled, skim off fat from top. Return soup to pot.
Add turkey meat to skimmed soup, along with herbs and spices.
Bring to a boil and add pastina. Continue cooking on low boil for about 20 minutes, until pastina is done. Serve at once or refrigerate for later reheating.
In a large soup pot, heat oil over medium heat. Add carrots, celery, and onion; cook and stir until the onion is tender.
Stir in garlic, oregano, basil, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in lentils and tomatoes, then add the vegetable broth and water.
Cover and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for at least 1 hour or until lentils are tender.
Store leftovers in the refrigerator and reheat on the stove or in the microwave. The soup will taste better the next day!
Combine olive oil, garlic, and chopped onion in a frying pan. Add chicken, and sauté together until chicken has browned.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, paprika, black pepper, and bay leaf, and stir to mix.
Bring to a boil. Simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, or until chicken is done.
Remove the chicken, and save the liquid in the pan. Arrange the chicken on a broiler pan. Broil until the chicken has nicely browned. Remove from the broiler, and place chicken in a serving bowl.
Boil the sauce in the uncovered pan until its volume is reduced to about half and the sauce is thick.
Pour the thickened sauce over the broiled adobo (chicken), and garnish with red tomato wedges, if desired.
Heat oil in a 4-quart saucepan.
Add garlic, onion, and celery and sauté about 5 minutes.
Add all remaining ingredients except spaghetti, and stir until ingredients are well mixed.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer about 45 minutes or until vegetables are tender.
Add uncooked spaghetti and simmer 2-3 minutes only. Serve warm.
In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.
While water heats and pasta cooks, warm olive oil in a large nonstick pan over medium heat.
Add pasta, and cook according to package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 8 minutes.
Chop the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. Cook the mushrooms in the oil for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice onion and mince garlic. Add to mushrooms. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add wine. Cook and stir to loosen any flavorful browned bits to mix into the sauce. Stir in chicken broth, salt, pepper, and thyme.
Drain pasta. Stir into mushroom mixture. Continue simmering mixture until all moisture is absorbed, about 3 minutes.
Divide into four equal portions (each about 1¼ cups). Top each with 1 tablespoon shredded parmesan cheese.
In a kettle, combine the yucca with enough cold water to cover it by 1 inch. Bring the water to a boil, and slowly simmer the yucca for 20 to 30 minutes, or until it is tender.
Preheat oven to 350° F.
Transfer the yucca with a slotted spoon to a cutting board, let it cool, and cut it lengthwise into ¾-inch-wide wedges, discarding the thin woody core.

Spray a cookie sheet lightly with the cooking spray. Spread yucca wedges in a single layer on the cookie sheet, and spray the wedges with cooking spray. Cover with foil and bake for 8 minutes. Uncover and return to oven to bake for an additional 7 minutes.
Cook the dried beans as directed on the package, until they are soft. Set aside.
Spray a large saucepan with nonstick cooking spray, and preheat over medium heat. Cook celery, onion, and green pepper until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, water, and seasonings to vegetable mixture. Bring to a boil. Add beans, and return to a boil.
Cover and cook over low heat until flavors are blended and liquid is absorbed away, about 15 minutes. Stir once in a while to prevent from sticking.
Serve with rice that is cooked without salt.
Preheat oven or toaster oven to 450 °F.
For each pizza, spread ¼ cup tomato sauce on a pita and top with ¼ cup chicken, ¼ cup broccoli, ½ tablespoon parmesan cheese, and ¼ tablespoon chopped basil.
Place pitas on a nonstick baking sheet and bake for about 5–8 minutes until golden brown and chicken is heated through. Serve immediately.
Mix the fruit together in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, combine all the ingredients for the honey orange sauce and mix well.
Just before serving, pour the honey orange sauce over the fruit.
Heat oil in a 12-inch sauté pan over medium heat. Cook onion, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes, until pieces begin to soften, but not brown.

Meanwhile, dice green pepper into pieces about ¼ inch in size. Tip: Slice pepper lengthwise into ¼-inch strips. Holding the strips together, cut crosswise in ¼-inch pieces. Add green pepper to cooking onion. Cover. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While the green pepper and onion cook, mince the garlic. Add garlic, cumin, and oregano to the sauté pan. Cook and stir for 1 minute.
Add broth and rice to sauté pan with green pepper and onion. Stir well, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain beans and rinse thoroughly.
Add beans to sauté pan. Stir well. Cover. Simmer for 5 minutes to heat beans and blend flavors.
Preheat oven to 450 °F. Cover a baking sheet with aluminum foil for easy cleanup.
In a medium bowl, toss the beets with the olive oil until well coated.
Spread beets on baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake 30–40 minutes. When done, beets should be easily pierced with a sharp knife.

While beets bake, grate the zest from the orange. Place in a small bowl. Cut the orange in half. Squeeze the juice (about ½ cup) into the bowl with the orange zest. (Use a large spoon to press the inside of the orange to extract more juice.) Add anise seeds (optional). Set aside.
When the beets are tender, return them to the tossing bowl. Pour the juice mixture over the beets. Mix well to coat, and serve.
Wash potatoes, cut in half, and place in saucepan of cold water. Cook, covered, over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes or until tender.
Drain and dice potatoes when cool.
Add vegetables and egg to potatoes, and toss.
In a small bowl, blend together the mayonnaise, mustard, salt, pepper, and dill weed.
Pour dressing over potato mixture and stir gently to coat evenly.
Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Spoon 1 tablespoon of yogurt into the bottom of each 8-ounce wine or parfait glass. Top the yogurt with 1 tablespoon sliced bananas, 1 tablespoon sliced strawberries, and ¼ cup graham cracker crumbs.
Repeat the yogurt, banana, strawberry, and graham cracker layers.
Top with a rounded tablespoon of fat-free whipped topping, if desired.
Serve the parfait immediately, or cover each glass with plastic wrap and chill for up to 2 hours before serving.
Place all ingredients in blender, and puree until smooth.
Serve in frosted glasses.

In a saucepan combine ¾ cup of water with the sugar, lemon juice, and lemon peel (and rum or vanilla extract if desired). Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and add the fruit. Cook at a very low heat for 5 minutes.
Pour the syrup into a cup and set aside. Remove the lemon peel and cool the cooked fruit for 2 hours.
To serve the compote, arrange the fruit in a serving dish and pour a few teaspoons of syrup over the fruit. Garnish with mint leaves (if desired).

recipes.title: Turkey and Beef Meatballs with Whole-Wheat Spaghetti

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 ºF.
In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.
Add pasta, and cook according to package directions. Drain.

Meanwhile, combine ingredients for the turkey and beef meatballs in separate bowls, and mix well. Measure 1½ tablespoons of turkey mixture and roll in hand to form a ball; then place the meatball on a nonstick baking sheet. Repeat, and follow same instruction for beef mixture, until eight turkey and eight beef meatballs are made.
Bake meatballs on a nonstick baking sheet for 10 minutes (to a minimal internal temperature of 165 °F).
Warm sauce, if necessary.
Serve four meatballs, ¾ cup hot pasta, ½ cup sauce, 1 teaspoon cheese, and a pinch of basil per portion.
Optional step: Bring the wine to a boil in a medium saucepan. Break up the mushrooms, then stir them into the wine. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Finely chop the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. Or you can coarsely chop them, place them in a food processor, and pulse until all vegetables are finely chopped.
In a 4-quart saucepan, bring 3 quarts of water to a boil over high heat.

While the water is heating up, warm the olive oil in a large nonstick pan over medium-high heat. Crumble in the ground turkey. Sprinkle with anise seed and salt. Cook for 5–10 minutes to brown, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, when the water comes to a boil, add pasta to boiling water. Cook according to package directions for the shortest recommended time, about 10–12 minutes.

Add vegetables to cooking turkey. Reduce heat to medium. Cook and stir 10 minutes until all vegetables are soft, but not browned. And tomato paste, and simmer for an additional 5–10 minutes. (Continue to optional step 7 if including the optional ingredients; otherwise, skip to step 8.)

Optional step: While the pasta and turkey mixture cooks, strain mushrooms, draining unabsorbed wine directly into the turkey mixture. Place mushrooms on a cutting board and chop finely, or place in food processor and pulse once or twice to more finely chop mushrooms. Stir mushrooms into turkey mixture. Simmer for 10–15 minutes to blend flavors.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to turkey mixture (the minimum internal temperature of cooked turkey should be 165 °F). Stir to blend well.
Divide pasta mixture evenly (about 2 cups each) among four dinner plates. Top each with 2 tablespoons of shredded parmesan cheese.
Preheat oven broiler on high temperature (with the rack 3 inches from heat source) or grill on medium-high heat.
To prepare burgers, combine ground turkey, scallions, pepper, and egg, and mix well. Form into ½- to ¾-inch thick patties, and coat each lightly with olive oil.
Broil or grill burgers for about 7–9 minutes on each side (to a minimum internal temperature of 160 °F).
Combine mayonnaise and mustard to make a spread.
Assemble ¾ tablespoon spread, 1 ounce spinach or arugula, several slices of grilled portabella mushroom (optional), and one burger on each bun.

recipes.title: Tuscan Beans With Tomatoes and Oregano

steps.text: In a large salad bowl, combine beans and tomatoes.

In a small bowl, combine olive oil, vinegar, oregano, pepper, and salt-free seasoning blend. Using a wire whisk, beat the ingredients until they blend into one thick sauce at the point where the oil and vinegar no longer separate.
Pour the dressing over the beans and tomatoes, and mix gently to coat.
Line four salad bowls with one romaine lettuce leaf each.
Top each leaf with one-fourth of the bean mixture, and serve.
Put water and bouillon in a large pot, and bring to a boil.
Add potatoes and carrots, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients, except for tomatoes, and continue cooking for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Remove the four large chunks of squash and puree in a blender. Return pureed mixture to the pot, and let cook for 10 minutes more.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let sit for 10 minutes to allow stew to thicken before serving.
Toss first six ingredients in a large bowl.
Soak one rice paper wrapper in warm water until soft (1 to 2 minutes). Shake off excess water.
Place vegetable filling off-center on rice paper, and fold like an egg roll (tuck in the sides to keep the filling inside).
Repeat with remaining vegetable filling and rice paper wrappers.
Once you have assembled all of the spring rolls, serve immediately.
Heat canola oil in a large wok or sauté pan over medium heat. Add garlic, ginger, and scallions, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add water chestnuts, and continue to cook until they begin to soften, another 1–2 minutes.
Add vegetables, and toss until heated through, about 2–3 minutes (or up to 5 minutes for frozen vegetables).
Add rice, and continue to cook until hot, about 3–5 minutes.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss well, and serve.
Place all ingredients except the cheese in a microwave-safe 2-quart casserole dish.
Microwave on high for 7 to 10 minutes, or until vegetables are fork tender.
Add the cheese, and microwave on high for 30 seconds.
Let stand for 2 to 3 minutes before serving.
Heat the oil and fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, chilli powder and cumin and cook for a minute.
Add the beef and brown it, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the tomatoes and kidney beans, then simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Season to taste and serve with rice.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper until no streaks of white remain.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat until it foams.
Pour in the eggs. As they set, push the edges to the middle with a spatula and tilt the pan so raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is still slightly soft, scatter the cheese over one half.
Fold the omelette in half, slide it onto a plate and serve straight away.
Mix the soy sauce and honey in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through. Lift it out.
Add the broccoli, sliced pepper, garlic and grated ginger and stir-fry for 3 minutes, adding a splash of water if it catches.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and toss for a minute until glossy.
Serve over rice.
Heat the oil and fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir for a minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and chickpeas and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, season, and serve with rice.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat.
Add the peas and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Push everything to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble them until just set.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking up any clumps, until piping hot.
Stir in the soy sauce and sliced spring onions, then serve.
Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth, thin batter and rest it for 10 minutes.
Heat a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Pour in just enough batter to coat the base, swirling the pan. Cook for a minute until golden underneath, then flip and cook for 30 seconds more.
Serve with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of sugar.
Melt the butter in a large pan and soften the sliced leeks over low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the peeled, diced potatoes and the stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the milk and warm through.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta until just tender.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a pan and gently fry the sliced garlic for a minute without letting it brown.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Drain the pasta, keeping a splash of the cooking water, and toss it through the sauce, loosening with the water if needed.
Serve with torn basil and grated parmesan.
Boil the soaked cod for twenty minutes, drain, cool it and flake it, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil for eight minutes, add the thyme and the whole scotch bonnet: uncut, it gives aroma without heat.
Add the cod and tomatoes and cook through for five minutes.
Tip in the ackee, add black pepper and warm it two minutes, swirling the pan only. No spatula.
Lift out the chilli and serve with fried plantain, bread or boiled ground provisions.
Marinate the chicken in the soy with the crushed garlic and peppercorns for thirty minutes.
Lift the chicken out, dry it and brown it skin down. Keep the marinade.
Pour in the marinade, water and vinegar, add the bay and sugar. Bring it to the boil and neither stir nor cover for ten minutes.
Cover and simmer for twenty-five minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover and reduce the sauce for five to ten minutes, spooning it over the chicken. Serve with rice.
Beat the softened butter with the sugar until pale, about four minutes.
Sift the flour with the cocoa and salt and fold it in with a spatula to an even dough.
Add the cornflakes and fold them through in one movement, trying not to break them.
Drop the dough onto a tray by the spoonful and press each one down lightly.
Bake at 180 °C for eighteen minutes; the biscuits stay soft to the touch and firm up as they cool.
Cool them completely on the tray, without trying to lift them hot.
Whisk the icing sugar with the cocoa and hot water into a thick icing, coat the biscuits and press a walnut half into each.
Poach the chicken breast in salted water for twenty minutes and pull it into fine threads by hand.
Soak the crustless bread in the milk for ten minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add the ají paste and turmeric and cook five minutes.
Blend the soaked bread with its milk, the walnuts and the fried onion until smooth.
Return the mixture to the pan and cook it ten minutes on a low heat, stirring.
Stir in the chicken and parmesan, season and warm it five minutes to the thickness of soured cream.
Serve over boiled potato and rice, garnished with egg and olives.
Poach the chicken in two and a half litres of water with the spring onion and coriander for forty minutes. Lift it out and shred it; strain the broth.
Return the broth to the pot, add the small yellow potatoes and cook twenty minutes, until they collapse entirely and thicken the soup.
Add the other two potato varieties and the corn and cook twenty minutes more.
Add the guascas five minutes before the end: boiled long, they turn bitter.
Return the chicken, season, and serve with bowls of cream, capers and sliced avocado on the table.
Roast the peppers and aubergines at 220 °C or over a flame until blistered black all over.
Pile them hot into a covered pot for twenty minutes: the steam lifts the skin by itself.
Peel and seed them and leave the flesh in a colander for two or three hours. Do not press: the water should drain on its own.
Put it through a mincer or chop it by hand — not a blender: what is wanted is a coarse texture rather than a purée.
Reduce it in a pot with half the oil over a low flame for an hour, stirring every ten minutes.
Add the garlic, vinegar, salt and the rest of the oil and cook another half hour, until the oil starts separating. Pack it hot into sterilised jars.
Beat the softened butter with the icing sugar until pale, about four minutes.
Add the yolks one at a time, then the vanilla, zest and brandy.
Sift the cornflour with the flour, baking powder and salt and fold it in without long working.
Wrap the dough in film and refrigerate it an hour.
Roll it half a centimetre thick and cut four-centimetre rounds.
Bake at 170 °C for twelve minutes; the biscuits should stay pale, with only the underside going golden.
Cool them completely, sandwich them in pairs with dulce de leche and roll the sides in coconut.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Melt the butter with the golden syrup over a low heat, without letting it boil.
Dissolve the bicarbonate in the boiling water and pour it straight into the butter mixture; it foams up.
Pour the foaming mixture into the dry ingredients and stir until even.
Roll walnut-sized balls and set them on a tray with generous gaps between them.
Flatten each ball with your palm to a centimetre thick; they spread further in the oven.
Bake at 160 °C for twelve to eighteen minutes and cool them on the tray rather than a rack.
Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, oil and a pinch of salt for ten minutes, until smooth and very elastic. Oil it, cover it and leave it an hour.
Fry the breadcrumbs in half the butter until golden. Mix the apples with the sugar, cinnamon, raisins, lemon juice and zest.
Spread a cloth on the table, dust it with flour and stretch the dough with the backs of your hands from the centre outwards, until it is transparent. Trim the thick edges.
Brush the dough with melted butter, scatter the crumbs over a third of it and pile the apples onto them, leaving a border.
Roll it up by lifting the cloth — by hand the dough tears. Tuck the ends under, move it seam down onto a tray and brush with butter.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes, brushing with butter twice along the way. Serve warm, dusted with icing sugar.
Soak the purple corn in cold water overnight, keeping that water in the morning.
Grind the corn with its water in a blender to an even purple liquid.
Strain it through a fine sieve, pressing the pulp, and strain it a second time.
Add the remaining water, the cinnamon, cloves and orange peel.
Cook over medium heat for forty minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon, until it thickens.
Add the sugar and lemon juice and cook five minutes more.
Remove the spices and serve it hot in mugs, with a fried cheese pastry.
Peel the apples, cut them into thick wedges and spread them in a buttered dish.
Scatter half the sugar and the cinnamon over the apples and toss them lightly in the dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour with the remaining sugar and salt, using your fingertips, to a coarse crumb.
Mix in the oats and scatter the crumble over the apples without pressing it down.
Bake at 190 °C for forty minutes, until the top is golden and juice bubbles at the edges.
Warm the milk and cream with the split vanilla pod, without letting it boil.
Whisk the yolks with the cornflour, pour in the hot milk in a thin stream and cook the sauce to thickness, stirring.
Dissolve the salt in the warm water and stir in the flour by hand. Add the butter and cheese.
Knead for three minutes and let it stand five. The dough should stop sticking and roll into a ball easily.
Shape cakes ten centimetres across and a centimetre and a half thick. Smooth the edges with wet fingers; cracks widen in the pan.
Griddle them with a drop of oil for four minutes a side, to a firm crust.
Finish them at 180 °C for ten minutes. A done arepa sounds hollow when tapped.
Split them hot lengthways, not all the way through, and stuff them: cheese, avocado, stewed meat or egg.
Boil the beans, chickpeas and lentils separately until soft; each takes its own time.
Parboil the cracked wheat and the rice and drain them.
Fry the chopped onion in oil until golden and add the tomato paste and paprika.
Combine all the grains and pulses with the onion, season, and stir in the coriander.
Rinse the cabbage leaves of excess brine and pare down the thick ribs.
Roll the filling in the leaves into tight parcels, packing them in layers in a pot.
Add water to the level of the top layer, cover with a weighted plate and cook an hour on a low heat. Cool it completely.
Pour the coconut milk into a heavy pot and cook it over medium heat, stirring.
Keep cooking until the milk separates into oil and brown solids.
The moment the solids turn deep brown, add the water at once to stop the caramelisation.
Add the sugar, salt and raisins and bring it to the boil.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot in an even layer.
Cook uncovered over medium heat until the liquid falls to the level of the rice.
Cover it, drop the heat to its lowest and hold it twenty minutes without opening it once.
Rub the chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, garlic and lime juice and leave it half an hour.
Brown the chicken in olive oil on all sides and lift it out.
Sweat the onion, pepper and garlic in the same oil for twenty minutes, until completely soft; that is the sofrito.
Add the tomato sauce and the saffron steeped in a spoon of warm water and cook five minutes.
Return the chicken, add the beer and stock, bring it up and season.
Add the rice in an even layer, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without stirring.
Scatter the peas and olives over the top, cover and let it stand ten minutes before serving.
Light the firewood to one side of the grate and let it burn down to embers, about forty minutes.
Mix the parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar, oil and chilli flakes; the chimichurri needs an hour to stand.
Rake a thin layer of embers under part of the grate and lay on the sausages; they go first.
Salt the ribs coarsely all over and lay them bone side down over a moderate heat.
Cook the ribs bone down for two hours, adjusting the embers so a palm can stay above the grate for seven seconds.
Turn the ribs and give them forty minutes meat side down, for a crust.
Add the flank for the last twenty minutes, rest the meat ten and serve it with the chimichurri.
Pierce the meat in several places with a knife, rub it with salt, pepper and garlic and leave it an hour.
Melt the panela in oil in a heavy pot until nearly black, without stirring it with a spoon.
Lower the beef into the caramel and sear it on all sides to a black crust, about fifteen minutes.
Lift out the meat and fry the onion, pepper, carrot and leek in the same fat until soft.
Return the meat, add the tomatoes, wine, Worcestershire sauce and bay, and add water to half its height.
Braise covered for four hours on the lowest heat, turning the joint every hour.
Lift out the meat, strain the sauce, reduce it by half and slice the beef across the grain.
Knead a dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it forty minutes under film.
Chop the spring onion very fine, salt it and wring it out in a cloth.
Fry the onion with the mince, add the tomato paste and stew it twenty minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and salt and leave it at room temperature.
Roll the dough thin and cut eight-centimetre rounds.
Add the leek filling, fold each into a half-moon and crimp the edge tight.
Boil the dumplings five minutes, lay them on the yoghurt, spoon the sauce over and dust with mint and chilli.
Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, then add the tomato paste and coriander.
Add water, season and stew forty minutes, until the meat is tender.
Stir in the peanut butter and rain in the ground okra in a thin stream, stirring constantly.
Cook the sauce ten minutes; it turns thick and stringy.
Bring a litre of salted water to the boil, set a cup aside and rain in the flour, working it with a stick.
Work it fifteen minutes, adding the reserved water, until the mass is dense and smooth.
Turn the asida onto a platter with a wet spoon, make a hollow and pour the mulah into it.
Grind the garlic, ginger, chilli, stock cube, salt and oil into a paste.
Slash the fish at the sides and rub the paste inside the cuts and over the skin. Leave it twenty minutes.
Break up the attiéké with your hands, sprinkle it with hot water and salt it.
Cover it and let it steam ten minutes, in a steamer or simply covered somewhere warm.
Slice the onion, tomatoes and chilli and mix them with lemon juice, salt and a spoon of oil.
Grill the fish over coals or in a griddle pan, seven minutes a side.
Serve the attiéké, fish and salad on one plate, with a wedge of lemon.
Cover the chicken with two and a half litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and simmer forty-five minutes.
Lift out the chicken, strain the broth and return it to the heat. Cook the rice in it for fifteen minutes.
Pull the meat into threads, discarding skin and bones.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice to an even froth in a separate bowl.
Ladle hot broth into the egg and lemon mixture, whisking without stopping, until the bowl warms up.
Pour the mixture back into the pot off the heat, return the meat and warm it through without boiling.
Poach the soaked cod for five minutes, cool it and pull it into flakes by hand, discarding skin and bones. By hand rather than with a fork: that is how small bones are found.
Deep-fry the potato matchsticks at 180 °C to a crisp gold, in batches. Drain on a rack and salt them.
In a wide pan sweat the onion in the olive oil for ten minutes until soft and sweet, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the cod and warm it through for three minutes, then tip in the potato and toss.
Take the pan off the heat, pour in the beaten eggs and stir without stopping for half a minute, until they turn creamy. Scatter over the parsley and olives.
Make the syrup: bring the sugar and water to the boil, cook fifteen minutes, add the lemon juice and cool it completely.
Melt the butter and let it settle — use only the clear upper layer and discard the sediment.
Lay twenty sheets into a greased tin, brushing each with butter. Scatter the pistachios in an even layer.
Cover with twenty more sheets, brushing each in the same way. Butter the top sheet especially generously.
Cut it into diamonds with a sharp knife, right down to the base of the tin.
Bake at 170 °C for an hour, to a deep gold. Take it out and pour the cold syrup into the cuts at once.
Leave it six hours, better overnight. Cutting and serving earlier is pointless: the syrup has not reached the lower layers.
Rub the flour with the fat and salt to a crumb, add the hot water and knead a soft dough.
Divide it into eight balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under a cloth.
Fry the onion in oil, add the cooked beans with some of their liquid and mash them smooth.
Fry the purée over medium heat for ten minutes, until it holds its shape on a spoon.
Roll the balls into thin twenty-centimetre rounds.
Cook them on a hot dry pan a minute a side, to spotted but not dried out.
Spread beans over half the tortilla, add cream and cheese, fold it over and serve hot.
Beat the softened butter with the sugar with a wooden spoon for twenty minutes, to a pale fluffy mass.
Add the yolks one at a time, still beating in the same direction.
Add the vanilla, salt and soda and beat five minutes more.
Work in the cornmeal a little at a time, to a firm but pliable dough.
Rest the dough fifteen minutes so the meal takes up the moisture.
Shape walnut-sized balls and set them well apart on parchment.
Bake at 170 °C for twenty minutes, to a pale gold edge, and cool them on the tray.
Boil the beans with the chopped green plantain for an hour and a half, until soft and thick.
Simmer the pork belly in salted water for forty minutes and dry it thoroughly.
Fry the belly skin down in deep oil until the skin blisters and crisps.
Make the hogao: fry the onion with the tomato and cumin, add the mince and cook it through.
Fry the chorizo, cook the rice and fry slices of ripe plantain to a caramel colour.
Cook the arepas on a dry pan and fry the eggs with runny yolks.
Build the tray: beans, rice, mince, chicharrón, chorizo, egg, arepa, plantain and avocado side by side.
Stir the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt into 100 ml of warm water until dissolved. Pour it over the carrot and daikon and leave for an hour at room temperature.
Marinate the pork in fish sauce with a spoon of sugar for twenty minutes, then sear it over a high flame for three minutes a side, until the edges caramelise.
Warm the baguettes at 200 °C for five minutes so the crust crisps again. Split them lengthways, not all the way through.
Spread pâté on one half and mayonnaise on the other. Layer in the pork, the drained pickles, cucumber, coriander and chilli. Press it shut with your palm and serve at once.
Crush the cheese with a fork and work in four of the eggs: the filling should stay crumbly rather than becoming a paste.
Mix the melted butter with the sunflower oil: that lets the sheets crisp without burning.
Lay two overlapping filo sheets, brush with the fat, scatter the filling in a crumbly line along the long edge and roll it loosely.
Coil the roll into a round tin from the centre outwards, leaving a couple of millimetres between the turns.
Whisk the yoghurt with the last egg and the bicarbonate and pour it over, aiming into the gaps between the coils.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, to a deep gold. Cover with a cloth for ten minutes out of the oven.
Mix the maize and cassava doughs with a litre of water and salt to a smooth, lump-free batter.
Set it over medium heat and work it with a wooden paddle without stopping. It starts to thicken after five minutes.
Keep working it for twenty minutes, pressing it against the sides, until it turns dense and glossy.
Shape balls with wet hands and wrap each in film or a banana leaf.
Rub the fish with salt, ginger and garlic and grill or pan-fry it eight minutes a side.
Grind the tomatoes, habaneros, onion, salt and a spoon of oil in a mortar to a coarse sauce.
Serve a ball of banku, the fish and a bowl of sauce. It is eaten by hand, pinching off dough and dipping it.
Cut three slashes on each side of the fish and pat it completely dry.
Work the garlic with the butter, lemon myrtle, lime zest, salt and pepper.
Rub the mixture into the slashes and the cavity and tuck slices of lime and fennel inside.
Wrap the fish in foil with the seams on top so the juices do not run out.
Light the coals and rake them to the sides; the heat under the fish has to be indirect.
Cook it in the foil for twenty minutes, turning the parcel once halfway.
Unwrap it, move the fish onto an oiled grate over the coals and give it a minute a side for the crust.
Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Work in the eggs, melted butter, salt and flour to a soft dough. It should stay slightly tacky.
Cover and leave somewhere warm for an hour, until the dough has doubled.
Knock it back, roll it out a centimetre and a half thick and cut it into three-centimetre squares or diamonds.
Let the pieces stand under a cloth for twenty minutes; this second rise is the reason for the hollow.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry in batches for two to three minutes, turning, to an even gold.
Drain on paper and serve warm, with tea, soured cream or honey.
Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, boil two minutes and drain; this removes the scum.
Fry the ginger, garlic and doubanjiang in oil for five minutes, until the oil turns red.
Add the tomatoes, wine and soy sauce, cook three minutes and return the meat to the pot.
Add water two fingers above the meat, drop in the star anise, cinnamon and sugar and simmer two hours.
Lift out the meat, cut it into thick slices and return it to the broth for ten minutes.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot of clean water and blanch the bok choy.
Divide the noodles between bowls, add the meat and greens, ladle over the broth and top with pickled mustard greens and spring onion.
Cut the beef across the grain into centimetre strips, pat them dry and pepper them.
Heat a pan hard and sear the beef in batches for ninety seconds, without turning it often.
Lift out the meat and fry the mushrooms over a high flame until their water has gone.
Add the butter and onion and fry until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the stock, stirring until smooth.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the soured cream and mustard, and season.
Return the meat with its juices, warm it a minute without boiling and scatter with parsley.
Simmer the chicken and veal with the onion, carrot and celeriac for an hour, skimming.
Lift out the meat, strain the broth and pull the chicken into fine threads.
Rinse the okra under cold water and pat it dry without trimming the caps.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes without letting it colour.
Pour the broth into the roux, add the okra and cook fifteen minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the soured cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring without stopping.
Take the pot off the heat, pour in the mixture, return the meat and warm it through without boiling. Add lemon and parsley.
Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes, until it foams.
Knead a dough from the flour, yeast mixture, eggs, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt.
Work in the softened butter in stages, kneading until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour and a half, until doubled.
Work the pearl sugar in by hand, distributing it evenly but without long kneading.
Divide the dough into ten lumps and rest them fifteen minutes.
Bake them in the iron three minutes each, to a deep gold with a caramel crust.
Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim, and simmer on the lowest heat for two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it under film for forty minutes.
Roll the dough a millimetre thick and cut it into squares of about eight centimetres.
Slice the onion into rings, pour a ladle of hot broth over it and leave it ten minutes; this is the sorpa that dresses the dish.
Lift out the meat, skim the fat into a separate bowl and boil the dough squares in that broth in batches, three to four minutes each.
Pull the meat apart into thin sheets across the grain. Lay the dough on a large platter, the meat on top, the onions and their broth over that.
Serve the remaining broth hot in bowls with herbs; it is drunk before the dish or alongside it.
Cover the meat with cold water, bring it up, skim and simmer two and a half hours with the peppercorns and bay.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, eggs, water and salt and rest it forty minutes.
Roll it a millimetre thick and cut it into diamonds six centimetres across.
Render the mutton fat and cook the sliced onion in it until soft.
Add two ladles of broth to the onion and stew ten minutes into a thick gravy; that is the chyk.
Boil the dough diamonds in the strained broth in batches, four minutes each, and plate them straight away.
Pull the meat into sheets, lay it over the dough, spoon the chyk over and scatter with coriander. Serve the broth in bowls.
Dry-roast the moong dal for five minutes, to a nutty smell, and rinse it.
Rinse the rice and dry it. Wet rice will not toast; it steams in its own water.
Heat the ghee, brown the potatoes and lift them out.
In the same ghee fry the bay, cinnamon and cardamom, then the onion and ginger until golden.
Add the rice and dal with the turmeric and cumin and toast them five minutes, stirring.
Add boiling water at twice the volume of the grain, return the potatoes, season and add the whole chillies.
Cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat, then let it stand ten minutes without opening it.
Soak the dried mushrooms in a cup of warm water for half an hour and slice them, straining and keeping the water.
Squeeze the sauerkraut, shred the fresh cabbage and stew each in its own pot for thirty minutes.
Render the bacon to crackling, brown the pork and beef in its fat, then the onion.
Combine both cabbages, the meats, sausage, mushrooms with their water, prunes, tomato paste and spices in a large pot.
Add the wine, bring it up and stew two hours on the lowest heat, stirring occasionally.
Cool it completely and leave it a day in the cold, then bring it back to the boil and stew an hour.
Repeat the cycle once more on the third day. Serve with rye bread and a glass of vodka.
Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave it ten minutes.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, eggs, yeast mixture, salt and two spoons of ghee, and work it fifteen minutes.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Divide it into ten balls, oil them and rest them twenty minutes under film.
Stretch the first ball by hand to the size of the tin, lay it in and brush it generously with ghee.
Repeat with the rest, buttering every layer. Brush the top one too and scatter it with nigella.
Bake at 190 °C for thirty-five minutes and pour the honey over immediately, while the bread is hot.
Cover the oats with water or apple juice and leave them overnight in the fridge.
In the morning stir in the yoghurt, cream and condensed milk until even.
Grate the apples, skins and all, on a coarse grater straight into the bowl.
Squeeze lemon juice over the grated apple at once and stir it through so it does not brown.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan for five minutes and chop them coarsely.
Stir in the honey, divide it between bowls and top with the nuts and berries.
Simmer the beef in the stock for ninety minutes, until completely tender, and shred it fine.
Fry the onion in butter, stir in the flour and cook it three minutes without letting it colour.
Pour in the hot stock in a thin stream and cook it to a very thick paste, about ten minutes.
Stir in the meat, parsley, nutmeg, salt and pepper, spread it in a dish and chill it four hours.
Roll the set mixture into walnut-sized balls with damp hands.
Coat them in flour, egg and crumbs, chill them twenty minutes, then repeat the egg and crumbs.
Fry at 180 °C for three minutes, to a deep gold, and serve with mustard.
Soak the bread in half the milk for ten minutes and squeeze it out, keeping the milk.
Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the curry powder and turmeric and warm them a minute, until fragrant.
Add the mince and cook, breaking up lumps, until it loses its pink, about ten minutes.
Stir in the bread, apricots, raisins, chutney, vinegar, salt and pepper and take it off the heat.
Press it into a dish, level it and bake at 180 °C for forty minutes.
Beat the eggs with the remaining milk, pour it over, stand the bay leaves in the custard and scatter the almonds.
Return it to the oven for twenty minutes, until the custard sets and turns golden.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil and salt.
Cover the dough and rest it thirty minutes.
Boil the potatoes soft, drain them and mash them without milk.
Work the spring onion, coriander, chilli, salt and pepper into the mash.
Divide the dough into six and roll each into a thin round.
Spread the filling thinly over half the round and fold the other half over, pressing the edge.
Cook them on a brush-oiled pan, four minutes a side, until spotted.
Dissolve the yeast with the sugar in the warm milk and leave it fifteen minutes, until it foams.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, sponge, egg, melted butter and salt.
Let it rise somewhere warm for an hour, until doubled.
Knock the dough back and roll it out to exactly a centimetre thick.
Cut it into four-centimetre diamonds and let them rest twenty minutes.
Heat the oil to 180 °C and lower the diamonds in in small batches.
Fry them a minute and a half a side, turning with a slotted spoon, to golden puffs.
Cover the meat with cold water, bring it to the boil and skim. Simmer for an hour and a half at a bare tremble — a rolling boil turns the stock cloudy.
Braise the beetroot in a pan with a spoon of oil, the tomato paste and the vinegar, covered, for about twenty minutes. The vinegar is what keeps the colour.
Separately fry the onion and carrot until soft and golden.
Lift the meat out, pull it into pieces and return it to the stock. Add the potatoes and give them ten minutes — before any acid reaches the pot.
Add the cabbage, then after five minutes the beetroot and the fried vegetables. Give it five minutes more, add the bay and garlic and take it straight off the heat.
Let it stand covered for at least twenty minutes. Serve with sour cream, which softens the acid and pulls the flavours together.
Make a stock from the ribs: an hour and a half at a bare simmer, skimmed. Lift the meat out and pull it apart.
Braise the beetroot separately with a spoon of oil, the tomato paste and the vinegar, covered, for twenty minutes. The vinegar is what holds the colour.
Fry the onion and carrot until soft. Put the potatoes into the stock and give them ten minutes, before any acid reaches the pot.
Add the cabbage, then after five minutes the beetroot, the fried vegetables and the beans. Give it five minutes.
Pound the salo with the garlic and herbs to a paste and stir it into the pot. Take it straight off the heat and let it stand covered for twenty minutes.
Cut all the vegetables into large pieces; they have to survive four hours without collapsing.
Line the bottom of the pot with the diced pork fat, put the meat on it and season.
Layer on the onion, carrot, parsley root, potato, peppers, cabbage and tomato.
Tuck in the whole head of garlic and the bay leaves, pour in the wine and add water to half the height of the pot.
Cover and put it in a 150 °C oven for four hours. Do not open it and do not stir.
Serve straight from the pot, digging to the bottom so every layer reaches the plate.
Soften the onion, leek and fennel in olive oil for ten minutes.
Add the small fish whole, the tomatoes, garlic, zest and saffron and cook five minutes.
Add two litres of water, bring it up and cook forty minutes, uncovered.
Press everything through a sieve, working the flesh through, and return the broth to the pot.
Cook the potatoes in the broth for fifteen minutes, then add the larger fish in order, firmest first.
Make the rouille: egg yolk, garlic, saffron, a pinch of cayenne and olive oil in a thin stream.
Serve the broth in bowls with croûtes and rouille, and the fish with the potatoes on a separate platter.
Mix the mashed potato with the tuna, chopped onion, capers, parsley, harissa, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Test with a scrap of pastry: it should surface at once and sizzle.
Lay a sheet on a plate, put two spoons of filling on one half and make a hollow in it.
Break an egg into the hollow, season it and fold the sheet over immediately, pressing the edges.
Slide the brik into the oil and fry forty seconds a side, steadying it with a slotted spoon.
Drain on paper and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly; only a little water should go, as a dry mass will not bind.
Mix in the flour, egg and salt. The mass should slide off a spoon slowly rather than pour.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Push the dough into boiling salted water through a colander with large holes. The dumplings are done when they float, after about three minutes.
Drain the dumplings, return them to the warm pan and stir in the brynza with a spoon of the cooking water. Keep the heat off.
Serve into bowls, spoon over the hot fat and scatter the crackling on top.
Put the guanciale into a cold dry pan and turn on a medium flame. A slow start renders the fat completely; a hot pan burns the outside and leaves it tough within.
When the pieces turn glassy and gold at the edges, lift half of them out for the top. Pour in the wine and let it cook away.
Crush the tomatoes by hand, add them with the chilli and simmer for ten minutes. The sauce should thicken without losing its red.
Boil the bucatini a minute short, move it into the sauce with a ladle of its water and finish it over the flame for half a minute.
Off the heat, stir in the pecorino and serve. The reserved guanciale goes on top with a little more cheese.
Dry the wings with kitchen paper, salt them and leave them uncovered on a rack in the fridge for at least four hours, better overnight.
Dust with the baking powder and toss so the coating is thin and even. Too much leaves a soapy taste.
Spread them on a rack over a tray and bake at 120 °C for twenty minutes: the fat renders out.
Raise the oven to 220 °C and bake another twenty-five minutes, to a deep gold and a crisp.
Melt the butter, take it off the heat and whisk in the pepper sauce, vinegar and garlic powder to an even emulsion.
Toss the hot wings with the sauce in a bowl and serve immediately with celery and blue cheese dip.
Marinate the belly slices and the mince separately in fish sauce, sugar, shallot, garlic and pepper for an hour.
Shape the mince into flat patties a centimetre thick; they cook fast and evenly.
Slice the papaya and carrot thin and pickle them in vinegar with sugar for twenty minutes.
Mix the fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, water, garlic and chilli and warm it through; that is the nước chấm.
Boil the vermicelli two minutes, rinse it in cold water and divide it between plates.
Grill the belly and the patties over coals, three minutes a side, to caramelised edges.
Drop the hot meat straight into the warm sauce with the pickles and serve with the noodles, lettuce and herbs.
Fry the onion in oil until deep gold and add the cinnamon, cardamom and curry leaves.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and the curry powder and cook them two minutes.
Add the lamb and brown it, turning it through the spices.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season and stew covered for an hour on a low heat.
Add the potato in large pieces and stew twenty-five minutes more.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until a spoon leaves a trail in it.
Halve the loaves, pull out the crumb, fill them with the curry and set the crumb on top.
Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, a spoon of oil, the vinegar and salt, and work it fifteen minutes until elastic.
Divide it into four balls, oil them, cover and leave them forty minutes.
Mix the raw mince with the onion, salt, pepper and two spoons of water; the water keeps the filling from drying out.
Stretch a ball by hand on a cloth-covered table into a translucent sheet, working from the centre outwards.
Sprinkle the sheet with oil, lay the filling in a line along one edge and roll it into a long thin cylinder.
Coil the cylinders into a round tin from the centre outwards, brush with oil and bake at 200 °C for forty minutes.
Sprinkle the hot burek with water and cover it with a cloth for five minutes to soften the crust. Serve with yoghurt.
Rinse the tripe several times, rub it with salt and rinse it again until completely clean.
Boil the tripe in water with half the vinegar for ten minutes and throw away that first water.
Cover it with fresh water and the bay and simmer three hours, until completely tender.
Boil the beans separately until soft, an hour and a quarter, and set them aside with their liquid.
Fry the pancetta and the sliced chorizo, add the onion, carrot and celery and sweat them ten minutes.
Stir in the paprika and tomatoes, add the sliced tripe with some of its broth and the potato.
