Spread the onion in an even layer over the base of the tagine or a heavy pan: it keeps the chicken off the bottom and becomes part of the sauce.
Set the chicken on top skin up, pour the water down the side, cover and cook over a low flame for forty minutes without lifting the lid.
Add the preserved lemon peel in strips and the olives, cover and give it twenty minutes more.
Take the lid off and reduce the sauce for five minutes if it is still loose. Check the salt only at the end: the lemon and olives have already provided it.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it in salted water for an hour. That removes surplus starch and lets the grains grow longer.
Boil the rice in plenty of salted water for five to seven minutes: a grain should bend but snap under pressure. Drain and rinse with warm water.
Grind the saffron and steep it in two spoons of hot water. Mix a couple of spoons of the rice with the yoghurt and saffron: this becomes the crust.
Heat the fat in the pot, lay the potato rounds edge to edge, spread the rice and yoghurt mixture over them and pile the rest of the rice on top in a mound.
Make five holes down to the base with the handle of a spoon for the steam to travel. Pour melted butter over.
Cover with a lid wrapped in a cloth, five minutes on a high flame and forty-five on the lowest. Do not lift the lid.
Stand the base of the pot in cold water for a minute and the crust releases. Invert it onto a plate in one movement.
Peel the papaya and shred it into long fine strips with a knife or a som tam grater.
Pound the garlic and chillies in the mortar into a coarse paste.
Add the cut beans and bruise them lightly with the pestle.
Add the tomatoes and crush them until their juice runs.
Add the padaek, lime juice and palm sugar and mix with the pestle and a spoon.
Add the papaya and work the pestle, turning with the spoon, for two minutes, until the fibres soften.
Taste and adjust for sourness, salt and heat. Serve with sticky rice.
Simmer the pork with the onion and salt for an hour. Strain and keep the broth.
Toast the seeds, sesame, chillies and tomatoes in a dry pan and blend them with broth; that is the recado.
Cook the recado twenty minutes to thicken it and season.
Slake the masa harina with warm broth, add the melted lard and work it twenty minutes over a low heat.
Pass the banana leaves over a flame for ten seconds each so they turn pliable.
On a leaf spread the dough, then a piece of meat, a spoon of recado, a strip of pepper and an olive. Wrap in two leaves.
Stack the parcels seam down in a pot and steam them for an hour and a half.
Grate the cucumbers coarsely or dice them small and salt them.
Leave the cucumber ten minutes to give up its water, but do not pour that water away.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste so it does not turn up in pieces.
Grind the walnuts to a fine crumb, keeping a few larger pieces back.
Whisk the yoghurt with the cold water until even and add the garlic and walnuts.
Stir in the cucumber with its juice, the chopped dill and the sunflower oil.
Chill it an hour and serve with an ice cube in each bowl.
Peel the apples, halve them, core them and squeeze lemon over them.
Melt the sugar in a cast-iron pan over medium heat to an amber caramel, without stirring it with a spoon.
Take it off the heat and beat in the butter piece by piece, with the vanilla and a pinch of salt.
Pack the apple halves cut side up, tight against each other, in a circle.
Cook on the hob for twenty minutes over medium heat, until the apples sink and take up the caramel.
Cover with a round of puff pastry, tucking the edges down inside the pan, and prick it in several places.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, rest it five, and invert it onto a plate in one movement.
Drain the soaked beans, cover them with fresh water, bring it to the boil and drain again after ten minutes.
Cover them a third time, add one whole onion and boil an hour until soft, without salt.
Fry the sliced onion in oil until golden, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika and flour.
Pour off some of the bean water, leaving it level with the beans, salt them and stir in the onion mixture.
Transfer to a clay pan, arrange the dried peppers on top and scatter with mint.
Bake at 200 °C for forty minutes, until a browned crust forms on top.
Rest ten minutes and serve straight from the pan, scattered with parsley.
Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook it two minutes, to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt until completely smooth and add the flour mixture.
Spread the rice in an even layer in an earthenware dish and lay the meat and its juices on top.
Pour the yoghurt mixture over so it covers everything by a finger's depth.
Bake at 180 °C for fifty minutes, until the top browns and the middle still trembles slightly.
Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, garlic and oregano and roast it at 190 °C for forty minutes, dotted with butter.
Parboil the rice for seven minutes and drain it.
Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour and cook two minutes to a nutty smell.
Whisk the yoghurt with the eggs and salt, add the flour mixture and beat until completely smooth.
Stir in the rice. It takes up some of the moisture and keeps the custard from splitting.
Arrange the meat and its juices in a dish and pour the yoghurt mixture over.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, until the top colours and the centre still trembles slightly.
Score the prawns three times on the inner curve and straighten them slightly, so they do not curl into rings in the oil.
Combine the dashi, soy and mirin, bring them to the boil and take them off: this is tentsuyu. Serve it with grated daikon.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Only when it is ready do you mix the batter — not before.
Beat the cold egg into the iced water, tip in the flour and cornflour and stir with chopsticks for five or six strokes. Leave the lumps.
Dust the pieces in dry flour, dip them in the batter and lower them in three or four at a time. Fry ninety seconds to two minutes.
Drain on a rack, never on paper. Between batches skim the floating scraps of batter out of the oil: they burn and taint the flavour.
Pound the parsley, garlic, chilli and salt into the rof paste and press it into slashes cut in the fish.
Fry the fish three minutes a side and set it aside.
In the same oil fry the onion until soft, add the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add two litres of water, the tamarind and the vegetables and cook twenty-five minutes.
Return the fish to the pot for ten minutes, then lift it and the vegetables out and keep them warm.
Add the rinsed rice to the remaining broth — twice as much liquid as rice — and cook covered for thirty minutes without stirring.
Turn the rice onto a large platter with the fish and vegetables on top. Share out the caught layer from the bottom separately.
Brown the meat in oil, add the onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook five minutes, until it darkens.
Add a litre and a half of water, season and cook forty minutes.
Slacken the peanut butter with two ladles of the broth until smooth and lump-free.
Pour the paste into the pot in a thin stream, stirring continuously.
Add the vegetables in large pieces and the whole chilli and stew thirty minutes, stirring.
Wait for the peanut oil to rise to the surface, remove the chilli and serve with rice.
Whisk the yolks with half the sugar over a pan of boiling water, without touching the water, until pale and thick — about seven minutes. Take it off and cool to room temperature.
Fold the cold mascarpone into the cooled yolks with a spoon rather than a mixer. A mixer breaks the fat and the cream turns grainy — the first place tiramisu usually fails.
Whip the whites with the rest of the sugar to firm peaks and fold them into the cream in three additions, lifting from underneath.
Mix the coffee with the marsala. Dip each savoiardo for one second a side and lay them in a tight layer in the dish.
Spread half the cream, level it, then repeat the biscuit and cream layers. Cover and refrigerate for at least six hours, better overnight.
Dust with cocoa through a sieve right before serving. Do it in advance and the cocoa takes on moisture and goes blotchy.
Drain the prawns in a sieve and let them sit for at least ten minutes.
Mix the mayonnaise with the crème fraîche, chopped dill, horseradish, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chop the red onion as fine as you can and stir it into the dressing.
Fold the prawns into the dressing gently, taking care not to crush them.
Trim the crusts from the bread and fry the slices in butter until browned on both sides.
Pile the prawns onto each toast, top with a spoon of roe and a sprig of dill. Serve at once.
Peel the prawns, leaving the tails on. Keep the shells and heads: the broth is built on them.
Fry the shells in the pot for a couple of minutes until bright orange, cover with the water and simmer fifteen minutes. Strain.
Return the broth to the heat, add the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and let them steep at a low simmer for five minutes.
Add the mushrooms and the crushed chillies, then after two minutes the prawns. They are done the moment they curl into a C — beyond that they turn rubbery.
Take the pot off the heat. Add the fish sauce, lime juice and sugar, stir and taste. Adjust a spoon at a time until sour, salty and hot sit where you want them.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the coriander. Leave the lemongrass and galangal in the pot, or warn people not to eat them.
Mix the flour with the salt and baking powder in a large bowl.
Melt the lard and stir it into the hot water until even.
Pour the liquid into the flour and work it with a spoon until it cools enough to handle.
Knead by hand for ten minutes to a smooth elastic dough.
Cover it and rest it twenty minutes at room temperature.
Divide it into eight, roll each into a half-centimetre round and cut a slit in the centre.
Fry at 180 °C for a minute and a half a side and serve with sugar or dulce de leche.
Score the plantain skin lengthways and lever it off with a knife; a green one will not peel by hand.
Cut them across into three-centimetre pieces.
Crush half the garlic with salt and stir it into half a litre of warm water.
Fry the pieces at 160 °C for four minutes, until soft but not golden.
Flatten each piece with the base of a glass or a press to a centimetre thick.
Dip the discs in the garlic water for a second and pat them dry.
Fry them a second time at 190 °C for two minutes to a crisp shell, salt them and serve with a mojo of the remaining garlic, olive oil and lime.
Fry the onion and garlic until soft, add both minces and cook, breaking up lumps, for ten minutes.
Add all the spices, season, and pour in the stock.
Simmer gently for forty minutes, until the liquid has almost gone.
Stir in the mashed potato and cool the filling completely.
Line a tin with pastry, add the cold filling and level it.
Cover with a second sheet, crimp the edges, cut vents and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200 °C for fifteen minutes, then at 180 °C for forty more, to a deep golden crust.
Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for ten minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, the yeast liquid, eggs, sugar and salt for ten minutes, then work in the soft butter piece by piece. Prove for an hour.
Roll the dough out and cut two-centimetre ribbons. Butter the spits and roll them in sugar.
Wind a ribbon round each spit, overlapping by a third and pulling it slightly taut. Roll it on the table so the layers bond.
Brush with butter, roll in the sugar, nut and cinnamon mixture and bake at 190 °C for eighteen minutes, turning every five.
Let it cool three minutes and twist it off the spit. Hot, it tears; fully cooled, it sticks.
Knead a soft dough from the flour, baking powder, salt and warm water, working it ten minutes.
Cover it and rest it an hour; the dough should become pliable and stop springing back.
Marinate the chicken with the curry powder, garlic, thyme and salt and stew it with the potato for forty minutes.
Divide the dough into six balls, roll each one thin and brush it with oil.
Roll the round into a rope, coil it into a spiral and let it rest twenty minutes.
Roll the spirals out into rounds again and cook them on a dry pan a minute and a half a side, brushing with ghee.
Move the bread onto a board and beat it into soft rags with two spatulas. Serve with the curry.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, water and salt and rest it thirty minutes.
Roll it thin, brush with fat, roll it up and cut across into half-centimetre strips.
Separate the strips by hand and spread them on a board so they do not stick.
Sear the mutton in the fat over a high heat, then add the onion, carrot, potato and cabbage.
Add a cup of water, season and bring it to the boil.
Lay the noodles in an even layer over the meat without stirring, cover and hold twenty minutes on a low heat.
Take the lid off, add the garlic and toss everything together. Serve at once.
Peel the apples and core them without going through, so each forms a cup.
Make a syrup of water, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon, bringing it to the boil.
Lower the apples into the syrup and poach them twenty minutes on a low heat, turning them.
Lift the apples out with a slotted spoon and cool them completely, keeping the syrup.
Mix the ground walnuts with three spoons of the syrup into a pliable mass.
Fill the apples with the walnut mass, mounded, and set them in dishes.
Spoon over the remaining syrup and top with whipped cream and a walnut half.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour, egg, water and salt and work it fifteen minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it forty minutes; that is what makes it pliable.
Chop the lamb and tail fat by knife into a fine crumb.
Mix the meat with finely chopped onion, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll the dough until translucent and cut five-centimetre rounds.
Fold the dumplings, sealing the edge and bringing two corners together into a ring.
Cook them in the boiling broth for eight minutes and serve them in a bowl with katyk and coriander.
Mix the kefir with the bicarbonate and leave it five minutes, until it bubbles. Add the egg, salt and flour and knead for eight minutes.
Cover the dough and rest it half an hour. Meanwhile let the cherries drain in a colander.
Mix the starch with the sugar and toss the cherries in it right before shaping.
Roll the dough to two millimetres, cut discs, put three or four cherries on each and seal the rim dry, pressing the air out.
Boil in batches in a wide pot of salted water. Two minutes after they float, lift them out and butter them at once.
Rub the pork with salt, pepper, caraway and garlic and leave it an hour at room temperature.
Brown the pork in lard on all sides, add the onion and pour in water to half the height of the meat.
Braise covered at 160 °C for an hour and a half, basting every twenty minutes.
Knead a dough from the flour, warm milk with yeast, the egg and salt and let it rise forty minutes.
Fold in the bread cubes, shape two logs and boil them ten minutes on each side.
Stew the sauerkraut with onion, caraway and sugar for twenty-five minutes.
Cut the dumplings with thread and the pork into slices, and serve with the cabbage under the pan juices.
Boil the barley in salted water for forty minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Render the pork fat to crackling, add the onion and fry it golden.
Cool both the barley and the fat with onion completely, or the blood sets when they meet.
Strain the blood through a sieve and mix it with the barley, fat, marjoram, allspice and salt.
Rinse the casings and fill them two-thirds full, leaving room for the barley to swell.
Tie the sausages every twenty centimetres and prick them in several places with a needle.
Bake at 180 °C for forty-five minutes, dotted with butter, and serve with lingonberry jam.
Shred the cabbage finely and mix it with the tomatoes, onion, vinegar, lime juice and salt.
Leave the curtido to pickle at least an hour, stirring it now and then.
Cut the pork skin into squares, salt it and leave it twenty minutes.
Render the skin in its own fat over a low heat for forty minutes.
Raise the heat and fry ten minutes more, until the crackling puffs and turns crisp.
Boil the cassava in salted water until tender, having cut out the woody core.
Lay the cassava on a banana leaf, the curtido over it and the crackling on top, with the chilli.
Drain the soaked rice and grind it with the coconut milk into a smooth, loose batter.
Stir in the yeast, sugar, cardamom, salt and grated coconut.
Leave the batter to ferment four hours in the warm, until it is covered in bubbles.
Stir the batter and check the body: it should pour in a ribbon rather than drop in a lump.
Heat the dimpled pan and brush each well with oil.
Fill the wells three-quarters full and cook three minutes, until the edges set.
Turn the cakes with a skewer and give them three minutes more, to a browned sphere.
Brown the chicken pieces with the annatto on every side.
Add the onion, pepper, tomatoes and carrot and stew until the vegetables soften.
Pour in two litres of water, salt it and simmer forty minutes over a low heat.
Mix the corn flour with the grated cheese, egg, oregano and a pinch of salt.
Add a couple of spoons of hot broth and work it into a firm dough that holds its shape.
Roll walnut-sized balls, compacting each between your palms.
Drop the balls into the boiling broth, leave them five minutes unstirred and cook twenty. Scatter with parsley.
Rinse the sorghum leaves and boil them in a litre and a half of water for ten minutes; the water turns deep red.
Take the leaves out, add a pinch of soda and the beans and cook forty-five minutes, until nearly done.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and add it to the pot. The liquid should stand a finger above the rice.
Salt it, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without stirring.
Take it off the heat, leave it covered ten minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Fry slices of ripe plantain until caramel-coloured.
Serve with egg, gari, shito and plantain, all on one plate.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, bay and thyme for forty minutes and strain the broth.
Cut the leek, carrot and celeriac into fine julienne of equal length.
Sweat the vegetables in butter for ten minutes, without letting them colour.
Add the broth and the potato in batons and cook fifteen minutes.
Joint the chicken, return it to the pot and take it off the heat.
Whisk the yolks with the cream and ladle in hot broth, stirring, until the bowl warms up.
Pour the mixture back into the pot off the heat, warm it through without boiling, and add lemon and parsley.
Rinse the whitebait in cold water and drain it in a sieve for ten minutes.
Pat the whitebait dry with a cloth; excess water stops the fritter setting.
Whisk the eggs with the flour, salt and pepper until smooth and lump-free.
Fold the whitebait into the egg mixture gently, taking care not to crush it.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until it just sizzles.
Pour in a ladle of the mixture and spread it into a thin round a centimetre thick.
Fry a minute and a half a side and serve with lemon and buttered bread.
Beat the meat between two sheets of film to three millimetres. Use the flat side of the mallet, not the toothed one: teeth tear the fibres.
Beat the eggs to an even liquid without foam. Salt the meat and coat it in flour, then egg, then crumbs.
Do not press the crumbs on. The coating has to sit loosely; only then will it lift and puff.
Heat a centimetre of fat to 170 °C and lower the schnitzel in. Fry two minutes, swirling the pan the whole time so fat washes over the top.
Turn it and give it ninety seconds more, to gold. Drain on a rack and serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
Separate two yolks and rub them through the cold rice with your hands until every grain is coated. Beat the remaining eggs separately.
Heat the wok with a spoon of oil until it smokes, pour in the beaten eggs, let them set and break them into pieces. Set them aside.
Fry the prawns for ninety seconds, add the ham, carrot and peas and cook a minute more. Add them to the eggs.
Add the rest of the oil, tip in the rice and fry three minutes at full heat, tossing constantly. The grains should be jumping in the wok, not sitting in it.
Return everything to the wok, pour the wine down the side and add the soy, season and toss for thirty seconds more. Scatter over the spring onion.
Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper, pour it over the chicken and onions and chill for at least four hours.
Lift out the chicken, pat it dry and brown it in oil on all sides.
In the same pan cook the onion from the marinade over medium heat for twenty-five minutes, until golden and soft.
Pour in the remaining marinade and the stock and add the bay leaves and the whole chilli.
Return the chicken, cover and stew thirty minutes on a low heat.
Uncover and reduce the sauce ten minutes more until thick. Remove the chilli.
Serve with boiled rice, the onions piled over the chicken.
Knead a dough from the flour, warm water, oil, egg and salt for ten minutes to elasticity. Oil it and rest it half an hour.
Mash the curd with the eggs, soured cream and salt. The filling should be firm rather than pourable.
Stretch the dough on a cloth by hand until translucent, brush it with melted butter and spread the filling over a third of it.
Roll it up by lifting the cloth and cut it into eight-centimetre pieces, sealing the ends by pressing with the edge of your hand.
Boil them in salted water for five minutes after they float and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Lay them in a dish, pour the cream over, trickle on melted butter and bake at 200 °C for twenty-five minutes, to a browned top.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it twenty minutes.
Simmer the beef with half the spices for forty minutes, until tender. Keep the broth.
Fry the onion in oil over medium heat for twenty minutes, to a deep brown, almost black.
Add the garlic, ginger and the remaining spices and warm them two minutes.
Add the cooked meat and the diced potato, stir and warm through five minutes.
Add the rice, pour in broth at one and a half times the volume of the rice, and season.
Bring it up, cover and cook twenty minutes on a low heat without lifting the lid. Rest it ten minutes.
Cover the chicken with three litres of cold water, bring it up and skim.
Simmer forty minutes on a low heat with a whole onion.
Knead a stiff dough from the flour and eggs, roll it thin, let it dry and cut it into fine noodles.
Lift out the chicken and joint it, and add the carrot, pepper and potato to the broth.
After fifteen minutes add the noodles and cook five minutes.
Boil the borș separately, strain it and pour it into the soup. Cook five minutes.
Return the meat, season and stir in the lovage and parsley. Let it stand ten minutes.
Grate the potatoes finely and squeeze them lightly, leaving some moisture in.
Crush the garlic with salt into a paste and work it into the potato mass.
Add the egg, milk, marjoram, pepper and flour and stir to a loose batter.
Heat the oil over medium and pour in a ladle of batter, spreading it very thin.
Fry three minutes a side, to a deep golden crisp crust.
Drain them on a rack rather than paper and serve them at once.
Cut the veal into fine strips across the grain and pat them dry.
Heat a pan with butter and sear the meat in batches for thirty seconds, moving it onto a plate.
Fry the shallot and mushrooms in the same pan until their water has gone.
Stir in the flour, cook it a minute and add the wine, reducing it by half.
Add the stock and cream and reduce the sauce to a coating consistency, about eight minutes.
Return the meat with its collected juices, warm it a minute without boiling, and add lemon.
Scatter with parsley and serve with rösti set alongside rather than under the meat.
Marinate the lamb in yoghurt with the hawaij and salt for two hours.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it thirty minutes.
Fry the onion in ghee to a deep gold and set half of it aside.
Brown the meat with the remaining onion, add the tomatoes and cardamom and stew an hour.
Fry the potato rounds to a golden crust in a separate pan.
Boil the rice in salted water for seven minutes, to half done, and drain it.
Layer the meat, rice, potato and raisins, streak the saffron over and bake it covered for thirty minutes.
Render the bacon in a pot, soften the onion in it, add the garlic and marjoram and warm them for half a minute.
Pour in the stock, lower the sausage in whole and simmer for thirty minutes. Do not pierce it, or its juices leave too early.
Lift the sausage out, slice it and return it to the pot. Shake the starter in its jar and pour it in, stirring.
Warm it for five minutes without letting it boil hard, stir in the cream and taste. If it is not sour enough, add more starter; salt at the end.
Ladle into bowls, add half a boiled egg each and serve with horseradish. In Poland żurek often comes in a hollowed loaf.
In a small bowl, stir together the paprika, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Coat the drumsticks with the olive oil.
Sprinkle the drumsticks with the seasoning mixture, rubbing to coat evenly.
Preheat an air fryer to 400°F.
Place the drumsticks in the basket of the air fryer and cook for 10 minutes.
Use tongs to flip the drumsticks over and cook for 8 minutes.
Check the internal temperature for a doneness of 165-175°F. If not cooked through, cook for 2-5 minutes until done.
Serve warm. •   Remove the skin before cooking to reduce the fat content, if desired.
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray the inside of a 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the cumin, coriander, garlic powder, chili powder or chipotle powder, paprika, black pepper, salt, and cayenne (if using). Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering. Add the selected protein, selected vegetables, and the seasoning mixture.
Cook until the protein is cooked through (if applicable) and the vegetables are tender, about 8-12 minutes, stirring and breaking the protein into crumbles or shreds as needed.
Divide the mixture between the tortillas (about 1 cup each), then roll each tortilla up into a burrito.
Place the burritos in the prepared baking dish, with their sides touching. Spread the salsa over the top, then sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake until warmed through and the cheese is melted, about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, oil, and black pepper.
Add the apples and onion. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
Place the apple, oats, milk, water, cinnamon, and salt in a microwave-safe bowl. Stir to combine.
Cook on high power (default setting) in the microwave until thickened and bubbly, about 3-5 minutes, removing once or twice during the cooking time to stir.
Top with the selected nuts and sweetener (if using). Serve warm.
Add the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice or vinegar, and salt to a large mixing or serving bowl. Stir together to make a dressing.
Add the cabbage, carrot, raisins or dried cranberries, and apple. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Add the milk, apple, oats, egg, selected sweetener, and cinnamon to a microwave-safe bowl or large mug.
Stir with a fork to combine.
Microwave on high (default power) for 2 minutes, then stir with the fork.
Continue cooking until creamy, about 30-60 seconds.
Serve warm.
Place the carrots and potatoes in the bottom of a slow cooker.
Using a paring knife, make a series of small, parallel cuts across the length of the pork tenderloin.
Fill each cut in the pork tenderloin with an apple slice.
Place the apple-filled pork tenderloin on top of the carrots and potatoes in the slow cooker.
In a small bowl, make a glaze by whisking together the honey, soy sauce, mustard, balsamic vinegar, cinnamon, and garlic.
Pour the glaze mixture over the pork tenderloin.
Cover the slow cooker with the lid.
Cook on high for 3-4 hours, or on low for 6-8 hours.
In a large saucepan or other large pot, add the apples, pears, water, lemon juice, cinnamon, ginger, and salt.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the apples and pears are very soft, about 25-30 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Use an immersion (handheld) blender to blend the mixture into a smooth sauce, or use a potato masher for a chunkier sauce.
Taste and add maple syrup or honey if more sweetness is desired.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired. This sauce will keep in the refrigerator for up to 7 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
In a small bowl, whisk together the sour cream, parsley, and hot sauce or chili oil. Set in the refrigerator to chill.
In a separate small bowl, stir together the salt and pepper.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then sprinkle evenly with the salt-pepper mixture.
Heat a tagine, a Dutch oven, or a large stockpot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Place the chicken in the pan and cook until golden-brown but not cooked through, about 3-5 minutes on each side. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium, then add the onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the garlic and allspice. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes with their juice, apricots, and cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Return the browned chicken to the pan and cover with a lid, Cook until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature of 175°F), about 33-35 minutes.
Serve warm, with a heaping tablespoon of the sour cream mixture on top of each portion.
In a large mixing bowl, make a dressing by whisking together the peanut butter, vinegar, honey, ginger, lime juice, sesame oil, soy sauce or tamari, and black pepper.
Add the cabbage, bell pepper, carrot, jalapeño or serrano, scallions, and selected fresh herb.
Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving. This slaw will keep in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
Add the rice, broth, and ginger to In a medium to large saucepan or stockpot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook uncovered until the soup thickens, about 40-45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm, topping each portion with a quarter of the scallions (~2 tablespoons each), ½ tablespoon of the soy sauce, and ½ teaspoon of the sesame oil.
In a small mixing bowl, make a marinade by whisking together the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, scallion, garlic, ginger, lemon zest, and white pepper.
Transfer the marinade mixture to a quart- or gallon-sized ziptop plastic bag. Set the bag inside the bowl, then add the chicken to the bag and toss to coat with the marinade.
Seal the bag, squeezing out the excess air. Let sit for 1-4 hours (in the refrigerator if longer than 1 hour).
Fill a 9x13-inch baking dish about halfway with warm water. Place four wooden skewers in the water and set aside.
Heat the grill to medium-high heat or the broiler to high heat. If the broiler is in an oven, move one rack to the top.
After 15 minutes of soaking, remove the skewers from the water and thread the chicken onto the skewers. Discard the excess marinade.

Brush the chicken with the oil, then place on the grill or on a broiler-safe baking sheet under the broiler (top oven rack). Cook to an internal temperature of 165°F, about 8-10 minutes, turning every 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm, adding garnishes as desired.
In a small bowl, whisk 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of the vinegar, and 2 teaspoons of the maple syrup with the garlic powder and ginger. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tempeh and cook until lightly browned, about 4-6 minutes, stirring often.
Add the soy sauce mixture. Cook and stir for 2 minutes, then remove from the heat and set aside.
In the small bowl used previously, whisk the peanut butter and water with the remaining 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of vinegar, and 2 teaspoons of maple syrup.
Divide the tempeh mixture between the lettuce leaves, then drizzle with the peanut sauce.
Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
Add the broth to a large saucepan or stockpot and bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Place a separate large skillet or sauté pan on a different burner over medium heat.
Add the oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion to the pan with the oil and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the rice to the pan with the onion and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add ½ cup of the hot broth, salt and pepper. Bring to simmer and cook, stirring constantly, until the broth is absorbed.

Continue adding the hot broth about ½ cup at a time and cook, stirring constantly, until it is absorbed before adding more. Cook until all the broth has been added and absorbed, about 17-20 minutes, adding the asparagus once you have added about half of the broth.
Add the spinach and cook, stirring often, until wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the parmesan cheese and lemon juice or vinegar (if using), then serve warm.
Add the chocolate chips, cocoa powder, and milk to a small microwave-safe dish and stir to combine.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 15-30 seconds at a time, stirring before starting again, until the chocolate chips are fully melted.
Add the avocado, selected sweetener, vanilla, salt, and melted chocolate mixture to a blender or food processor. Blend until completely smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Peel the hardboiled eggs, then slice in half lengthwise.
Remove the yolks from the egg halves and transfer to a small bowl. Mash into small pieces with a fork.
Add the avocado, lemon juice or vinegar, oil, salt, and black pepper. Mash with the fork to combine, adding more lemon juice or vinegar and/or oil to adjust the flavor and consistency as desired.
Using two spoons, one to scoop and one to scrape, divide the egg yolk-avocado mixture between the egg white halves (~1 tablespoon each).
Sprinkle the paprika over the tops of the filled eggs.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
In a medium mixing bowl, make a marinade by whisking together the oil, vinegar, garlic, honey or maple syrup, lemon zest, basil, oregano, thyme, sage, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper.
Transfer the marinade to a quart- or gallon-size ziptop plastic bag.
Add the tofu and toss gently to coat with the marinade.
Seal the bag, squeezing out as much air as possible.
Place in the refrigerator and let marinate, at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil.
Remove the tofu from the marinade and place on the baking sheet in a single layer.
Bake until crispy, about 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through the cooking time.
Serve warm.
Preheat oven to 450°F.
Add the flour to a shallow dish. Add the egg to a second dish. Add the breadcrumbs, ¼ cup of parmesan, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper to a third dish.

Coat each piece of sliced eggplant lightly with the flour, then the egg, and then the breadcrumb mixture. Transfer the breaded eggplant slices to a wire cooling rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet and let sit for 5 minutes.
Spray the breaded eggplant lightly on both sides with nonstick spray and bake until tender and golden-brown, about 20-22 minutes, flipping halfway through the time.
Meanwhile, heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chopped eggplant and salt. Cook, stirring often, until lightly-browned, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the garlic, red pepper, and the remaining ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the eggplant is tender and the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
Combine the remaining ¼ cup parmesan and the Italian cheese in a small mixing bowl. Top the baked eggplant slices with cheese and bake until melted, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the eggplant slices to plates and spoon the sauce over the top. Serve warm, sprinkling each serving with 2 tablespoons of chopped basil.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat the inside of a 9x13-inch baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and set aside.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted or thawed.
Add the selected protein and green chiles. Cook until warmed through, then remove from the heat.
Pour the enchilada sauce into a shallow microwave-safe dish (e.g. glass pie dish, shallow bowl) and warm in the microwave, about 1-2 minutes.
Set up a station with the following items, in this order: tortillas, warmed enchilada sauce, prepared baking pan, protein-spinach mixture, and shredded cheese.

Working one tortilla at a time, dip one tortilla in the sauce to coat and then place in the baking pan. Add ¼ cup of the protein-spinach mixture, then roll into a tube. Push to the side of the pan or next to the previous enchilada. Repeat with 11 more tortillas and protein-spinach mixture.

Spread any remaining protein-spinach mixture over the enchiladas. Dip the remaining 6 tortillas in the sauce and layer over the top. Spread any remaining sauce over the top, then sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake uncovered until warmed through, about 25-30 minutes. Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spray the inside of an 8x8-inch baking dish or 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.
Add the pumpkin and eggs. Stir until the egg yolks and whites are combined.
Add the milk and vanilla. Stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish or divide between the muffin tin cups.
Bake until fully set, about 30-35 minutes in an 8x8-inch baking dish or 25-30 minutes in a 12-cup muffin tin. Center should be firm when tapped and not indent.
Let cool for 5 minutes before slicing or removing from the muffin tin, then serve warm or at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Spray a rimmed baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray, then set aside.
Add the butter to a small microwave-safe bowl. Microwave on high power (default setting) until melted, about 15-30 seconds. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Add the cooled melted butter and milk. Whisk to combine.
Pour the egg mixture into the prepared baking sheet. Tilt the pan to each side until the liquid covers the bottom.
Working quickly, place the slices of bread onto the baking sheet in a single layer, then flip the slices over. Let sit to absorb the egg mixture, about 1-2 minutes.
Bake until the bottoms of the bread slices are golden-brown, about 12-15 minutes.

With the pan still in the oven, switch the oven to broil on high. Continue cooking until the tops of the bread slices are lightly-browned, about 1-3 minutes. This happens quickly, so watch closely to make sure the bread doesn’t burn.
Serve warm.
Put the banana in a medium mixing bowl and mash with a fork.
Add the eggs and mix with the fork until well combined.
(Optional) Put the oats in a blender or food processor and blend until finely ground (skip this step if using quick-cooking oats).
Add the oats and cinnamon to the banana mixture. Stir to combine.
Heat a medium or large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the skillet, portion the mixture into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on one side until golden-brown, about 1-3 minutes.
Flip all of the pancakes over and cook on the other side until golden-brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 7-9 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm, topping as desired
In a medium bowl, stir together the chicken, carrots, and barbeque sauce.
Mix until the chicken and carrots are well coated with the sauce.
Spread half of the mayonnaise or Greek yogurt on the top halves of each bun or sandwich thin.
Top the bottom half of each bun or sandwich thin with half of the chicken mixture and two lettuce leaves.
Add the top bun.
Serve immediately, or warm briefly in the microwave before serving, about 15-30 seconds.
Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.

Add the unpeeled garlic cloves and the walnuts to the pan. Toast, shaking the pan occasionally, until the garlic cloves are softened and spotty brown and the walnuts are golden and fragrant, about 7-10 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside to cool.
When the garlic cloves are cool enough to handle, remove and throw away the peels, then chop into large pieces.
Place the basil leaves in a gallon-size ziptop plastic bag. Squeeze out the excess air and seal the bag closed.
Pound the basil in the sealed bag with the flat side of a meat mallet or a rolling pin until all the leaves are bruised.
Add the garlic, walnuts, basil, oil, parmesan, lemon juice, black pepper, and salt to a food processor. Puree until smooth, scraping down the bowl as needed.
Serve as desired.
Add the beef, carrot, sweet potato, and broth to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the vegetables are tender, about 20-25 minutes. Halfway through the cooking time, check to make sure the vegetables are still covered by broth. If not, add enough water to cover them.
Blend until completely smooth with an immersion (handheld) blender or transfer to a standing blender, with the center piece of the lid removed and covered with a hand towel or folded-up paper towel.
If the puree is too thick, add an additional 1-3 tablespoons of water or broth and continue blending.
Serve warm.
Heat a medium to large skillet over medium heat.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, salt, and black pepper. Cook until softened and lightly-browned, about 8-10 minutes. Set aside.
Add the walnuts to a food processor and pulse to break down into small crumb-like pieces.
Add the beans, beets, panko, garlic powder, coriander, cumin, and onion. Pulse until the mixture is crumbly.
Transfer the mixture to a large mixing bowl and add the egg. Mix until well combined.
Using clean hands that are slightly wet, divide the mixture into four equal portions and form each portion into a patty about 4 inches wide and ½-inch-thick.
Return the skillet to the stovetop over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil.
Working in batches if needed, cook the patties until crisp and well-browned, about 6-8 minutes on each side.
Serve warm, on the desired serving vessel and topped as desired.
Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot and add just enough water fill the area under the steamer.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-high to maintain a rapid simmer (just below boiling).
Add the beet wedges to the steamer basket and cover the pot with a lid. Cook until the beets are tender, about 12-17 minutes.
Remove the steamer basket from the pot and set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Pour the milk into the pitcher of a blender. Add the berries, selected sweetener, salt, and steamed beets.
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately. Leftovers may be frozen, thawing in the microwave at 30% power for 3-5 minutes.
Empty the package of pudding mix to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the milk and stir until thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Gather four serving glasses or parfait dishes. Divide the pudding and berries between each of the glasses, alternating layers of berries with layers of pudding.
Top each glass with 1 tablespoon of the almonds.
Serve immediately, or chill up to 3 hours before serving.
Add the frozen bananas, berries, cranberry-pomegranate juice, lime zest, and ginger to a food processor or high-powered blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
In a small (~2-cup) jar, bowl, or storage container, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt, and cinnamon.
Add the berries and stir to combine.
Cover with a lid or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator. Chill overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm briefly (about 1 minute) in the microwave.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt, selected sweetener, and cinnamon.
Divide the yogurt mixture between four individual serving bowls or storage containers (~1 cup each).
Top each bowl with 1 cup of the berries, 1 tablespoon of the hemp hearts, and 1 tablespoon of the flax meal.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the beans, corn, onion, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, vinegar, cumin, salt, and black pepper.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Taste and add more black pepper or lime juice, if desired.
Serve with tortilla chips or as a topping for tacos or grilled chicken.
Add the oats or bread cubes to a food processor. Pulse or blend on low speed until crumbs form.
Add the chilled black beans, egg, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, cumin, coriander, and soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce.
Pulse or blend on low speed until the mixture is partially mashed and holds together. It should not be pureed.
Using slightly wet hands, divide the mixture into three equal portions and form each portion into a patty.
Spray a large skillet with nonstick cooking spray and place over medium-high heat.
Once the pan is hot, add the patties and cook until they are well-browned and hold together, about 5 minutes per side.
Serve warm on their own, with a dipping sauce, or on a bun with your choice of toppings.
Wash the sweet potatoes and prick with a fork in several places. Wrap in parchment paper or a paper towel.
Microwave the sweet potatoes on high power (default setting) until tender all the way to the center, about 7-10 minutes, flipping halfway through the cooking time.
Set the sweet potatoes aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, combine the beans, tomato, oil, cumin, and coriander in a medium microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave the bean mixture on high power (default setting) until heated through, about 2-3 minutes.

When the sweet potatoes are just cool enough to handle, cut a slice in each sweet potato lengthwise, just enough to open it but not to cut all the way through. Press the ends of each sweet potato to make a well in the center.
Spoon the bean mixture into the well of each sweet potato.
Top each sweet potato with 1 tablespoon of the Greek yogurt and 1 tablespoon of the cilantro. Serve warm.
Add the blueberries, lemon juice, and sweetener to the pitcher of a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, adding some of the kombucha to assist with blending if needed.
Add the remaining amount of the kombucha to the blender or food processor and stir by hand or pulse briefly to combine.
Pour into two glasses, dividing equally between the glasses.
Serve cold, garnishing with lemon and/or fresh blueberries as desired.

Combine the oats and buttermilk in a medium mixing bowl and let sit, covered, in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. If you don’t have time to let it sit, microwave the oat-buttermilk mixture until the oats have absorbed the liquid and the mixture is batter-like, about 1-2 minutes).
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and baking soda.
Add the flour mixture, egg, melted butter, and blueberries to the oat-buttermilk mixture. Stir to combine.
Spray a nonstick skillet with nonstick spray and set over medium heat.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the skillet, portion the batter into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on the first side until bubbles form and pop on the top surface and the edges are dry, about 3-4 minutes.
Flip all of the pancakes over and cook on the other side until golden-brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 5-7 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm.
In a medium mixing bowl, mash the banana with a fork.
Add the eggs, flax meal, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Whisk together with the fork to combine.
Add the oats and blueberries, then stir to combine.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, then coat the inside of the pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Working ¼ cup at a time and around the perimeter of the pan, portion the batter into the pan, leaving at least ½ inch between each portion of batter.
Cook on the first side until bubbles form and pop on the surface and the edges begin to dry, about 3-5 minutes. Flip and finish cooking on the second side, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat steps 5-6 with any remaining batter.
Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.

recipes.title: Braised Cod and Green Beans with Pesto

steps.text: Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the green beans and shallot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the shallot starts to soften, about 1-2 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the salt and pepper and sprinkle both sides of each cod fillet with the mixture.
Spread the green beans into a flat layer in the pan and gently place the cod fillets on top.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the cod is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 4-6 minutes.
With a slotted spoon or spatula, transfer the cod and green beans to a serving dish. Cover with foil to keep warm.
Continue to cook the broth over high heat, uncovered, until it is reduced to about ½ cup, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the pesto.
Pour the sauce over the fish and green beans.
Garnish with lemon wedges if desired and serve warm.

recipes.title: Braised Mustard Greens with Red Beans

steps.text: Heat a large sauté pan or skillet over medium heat.
Add the nuts to the pan and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly toasted, about 2-5 minutes. Remove the nuts from the pan and set aside.
Add the oil to the now-empty pan and place over medium heat. Heat the oil until it is shimmering.
Add the onion and sauté until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, curry powder or turmeric, black pepper, and salt. Sauté until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice. Stir to combine.
Add the mustard greens to the pan and cook, tossing or stirring occasionally, until they begin to wilt, about 1-2 minutes. Work in batches if needed.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and cover the pan with a lid. Cook until the greens are tender, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the beans, scallions, and toasted nuts. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, bell pepper, broccoli, and black pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-7 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs together.

Move the vegetables to the sides of the pan and pour the eggs into the middle. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a rubber spatula as the eggs cook, keeping the eggs in the middle and the vegetables on the sides.
Once the eggs are cooked, mix in the vegetables and stir in the cheese. Remove the pan from the heat.
Top each warmed tortilla with a quarter of the egg mixture and 1 tablespoon of the salsa. Wrap into a burrito and set aside. Repeat with the remaining tortillas, egg mixture, and salsa.
Serve warm.
Place the wrap or tortilla on a clean flat surface.
Spread the peanut butter on one half of the wrap or tortilla and the fruit preserves on the other half.
Place the banana at the edge of the wrap, on the preserves side, along the line between the peanut butter and the preserves.
Roll the wrap or tortilla up around the banana, rolling towards the peanut butter side. The peanut butter should act like a glue and keep the wrap together.
Enjoy whole as a grab-and-go breakfast, slice into pieces to share, or serve as a side.
In a medium mixing or serving bowl, whisk together the oil, vinegar, mustard, salt, and black pepper.
Add the beets, orange, arugula, and mozzarella.
Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Add the mayonnaise and vinegar to a large bowl. Stir together until smooth to make a dressing.
Add the broccoli, onion, grapes, carrots, and almonds.
Toss together to coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.

recipes.title: Recipe Title Broccoli Sesame Noodle Salad

steps.text: Fill large saucepan or stockpot halfway full with water. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the pasta and cook 4 minutes, then add the broccoli to then continue cooking until the pasta is tender, about 4-5 minutes.
Drain the pasta and broccoli into a colander and briefly rinse with cold water.
In a large bowl, whisk together the vinegar, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, and garlic.
Add the pasta, broccoli, and carrot. Toss to combine.
Serve cold, chilling in the refrigerator if needed. Toss again before serving to recombine with the dressing.
Heat a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Add oil and heat until shimmering.
Add onion and carrots. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the flour and cook while stirring for 1 minute.
Add the broccoli, broth, milk, and mustard. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil then reduce heat to maintain a simmer and cook for about 5 minutes or until broccoli is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheese and pepper.
Serve warm.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, and salt.
Cook, stirring often, until the tomatoes release their juice and the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the zucchini and corn.
Increase the heat to high and cook, stirring occasionally, until the zucchini is just starting to soften and the corn is thawed, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the cilantro and lime juice. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
Heat butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, swirling to coat the bottom of the pan.
Add honey or brown sugar and cinnamon. Stir to combine with the butter.
Add the bananas and cook, gently flipping every 1-2 minutes until they are softened and coated with the butter-sugar mixture, about 4-5 minutes in total.
Serve warm.
Heat a medium-sized sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and allow it to heat up (about 20-30 seconds).
Add the onion and salt and cook until the onions are caramelized, about 20-30 minutes, stirring every 5-10 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and set aside to cool.
While the onions caramelize, add the Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, garlic powder, and white pepper to a small mixing bowl. Stir to combine.
Add the cooled caramelized onions to the yogurt mixture and stir to combine.
Serve immediately or refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, up to 7 days. Stir before serving to recombine.
Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the carrots, potato, coriander, salt, and cayenne. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the broth and water. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the carrots and potatoes are tender, about 20-25 minutes.

Transfer a third of the broth-vegetable mixture to the pitcher of a blender. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl. Repeat with any remaining broth-vegetable mixture.
Return the soup to the pot and place over high heat. Bring to a simmer, then remove from the heat.
Add the lime juice and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the cilantro or parsley.
Add the orange juice, oil, lemon juice, cinnamon, and salt to a medium mixing or serving bowl. Whisk together to make a dressing.
Add the carrots and raisins. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Grease a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, oats, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Stir to combine.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the sugar, yogurt, oil, eggs, and vanilla.
Add the yogurt mixture and the carrots to the flour mixture. Gently fold to combine.
Divide the batter between the prepared muffin tin cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way full.
Bake for 22-25 minutes. Press down gently on the top of one of the muffins to test for doneness. If it springs back up, the muffins are done.
Let the muffins sit in the muffin tin for 5 minutes, then remove and allow to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Serve room temperature or warm.
In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, sugar, vinegar, olive oil, sesame oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add the cabbage or coleslaw mix, carrot, and edamame. Toss to combine.
Serve cold, adding 2 tablespoons of the cashews and 2 tablespoons of the chow mein noodles to each portion right before serving.
Spray a large skillet or sauté pan with cooking spray and place over medium heat.
Add the eggs and cook to scrambled, stirring often. Transfer the scrambled eggs to a small bowl and set aside.
Increase the heat to medium-high and add the oil. Heat until shimmering.
Add the riced cauliflower and cook until most of the liquid from the cauliflower is evaporated, about 4-6 minutes.
Add the selected vegetables, scallions, and garlic.
Cook, stirring often, until the liquid is evaporated and the vegetables are not releasing liquid, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, sesame seeds, and scrambled eggs.
Cook, stirring constantly, until the soy sauce is absorbed, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm.
Add the peaches and cherries to a medium saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until the fruit mixture is warm and syrupy, stirring occasionally, about 10-12 minutes.
Serve warm or cold over Greek yogurt, pancakes, or oatmeal.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, water, cornstarch, vinegar, honey, ginger, garlic to create a sauce. Set aside.
Heat a medium skillet over medium heat.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from pan and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Add the vegetables and cook, stirring often, until fork-tender but still firm, about 6-10 minutes.
Add the sauce and cook, stirring often, until the sauce is heated through and slightly thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the cooked chicken and stir to combine.
Serve warm over the cooked brown rice.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the ground chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Add the diced tomatoes and their juice, tomato sauce, enchilada sauce, and cauliflower rice.
Bring to a simmer and cook until the cauliflower is tender.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the cheese until melted and well mixed.
Serve warm.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken and cook, stirring often, until cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 6-8 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Set the pan back over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, and mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the cabbage, broth, bamboo shoots, and water chestnuts. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the cabbage is tender, about 5-7 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and water with a fork to make a slurry.
Add the slurry, sugar, and black pepper to the vegetable mixture. Stir to combine.
Cook until a slightly thickened sauce forms, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to combine.
Serve warm, topping each serving with ¼ cup of the chow mein noodles.
Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium-low heat.
Coat the pan with cooking spray.
Add the onion and cook until soft, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, peas, celery, bell pepper, thyme, fennel seed, black pepper, turmeric, and paprika.
Cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and broth.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the couscous.
Cover the pan with a lid and remove from heat. Let stand for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chicken and cook until heated through.
Fluff with a fork, then serve warm.
In a medium mixing bowl, mix together the garlic powder, chili powder, cumin, and cayenne.
Add the raw chicken and toss to coat with the spice mixture.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken. Cook, stirring often, until the chicken is fully cooked and no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pan and place on a clean plate. Cover the plate with foil and set aside.
Return the pan to the stovetop and turn the heat up to high.
Add the remaining ½ tablespoon oil.
Add the onion and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, until crisp-tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Divide the chicken, onion-pepper mixture, tomato, avocado Greek yogurt, and salsa over the tortillas.
Serve warm.

Stove-Top: Heat medium sized pot over medium high heat. Add 1 tablespoon oil. Once hot, add chicken and sauté for 5 minutes. Add ginger, garlic, spices and salt. Sauté for another 5 minutes. Add the tomato sauce. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the coconut milk or yogurt. Serve warm.

Instant Pot/Electric Pressure Cooker: Set to sauté mode. Add oil. Once hot, add chicken. Sauté for 5 minutes. Add ginger, garlic, spices and salt. Sauté for another 5 minutes. Add tomato sauce and stir to combine. Set to manual pressure cook for 10 minutes, then quick release. Stir in coconut milk or yogurt. Serve warm.

Slow Cooker/Crockpot: Omit oil. Add chicken, ginger, garlic, spices, salt and tomato sauce to crockpot. Cook on high for 4 hours or low for 8 hours. Turn off, add coconut milk or yogurt. Stir to combine. Serve warm.
In a Dutch oven over medium heat, combine stock, tomatoes, kale, Italian seasoning, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Add pasta and chicken.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to simmer.
Cook covered until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Top with cheese and serve.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper and onion. Cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the garlic, chili powder, paprika, cumin, and cinnamon. Cook and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer, then continue cooking for 3 minutes, stirring often.
Add the beans and stir to combine, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer (steaming, little to no bubbling).
Cook until the flavors have blended, about 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line the bottom and sides of a 7x4-inch rectangle baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang of the paper on all sides. Set aside.
Add the graham cracker crumbs and melted butter to a small mixing bowl. Stir to combine.
Press the crumb mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan and bake for 8 minutes. Set aside, leaving the oven on.
In a medium mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to beat together the cream cheese, yogurt, egg white, sugar, flour, lemon juice, and vanilla until smooth, about 3-4 minutes.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour the mixture into the pan with the crust and bake for 25 minutes, covering the pan with foil after 20 minutes.
Allow to cool at room temperature for 20 minutes, then set in the refrigerator to chill completely, at least 3 hours.
Lift out of the pan by the paper and slice into bars. Serve.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Prepare a 12-cup (regular-size) muffin tin or mini muffin tin by spraying each cup with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon. Set aside.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the pumpkin puree, sugar, eggs, oil, and yogurt.
Add the flour mixture to the pumpkin mixture, along with the chocolate chips. Fold together gently until just combined.
Fill the muffin tin cups three-quarters-full with the batter.
Bake until the muffins bounce back when gently pressed, about 20-22 minutes for regular-size muffins or 13-15 minutes for mini muffins.
Cool slightly, about 5 minutes, then remove from tin. Serve warm or place in an airtight container when completely cool. Keep at room temperature for 5-7 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months.
Add the oats and hazelnuts or almonds to the bowl of a food processor. Pulse or blend on low until finely ground into a powder.
Add the beans, chocolate-hazelnut spread, and vanilla extract. Pulse to chop the beans into small pieces.
Blend until the mixture resembles a thick dough, about 4-6 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Line a baking sheet or casserole dish with parchment paper or wax paper, then place it next to the food processor.
Carefully remove the blade from the food processor, then use a 2-tablespoon disher (spring-loaded cookie scoop) to portion the mixture onto the baking sheet.
Use clean hands to gently roll each portion into a ball.
Place the truffles in the refrigerator to chill, at least 1 hour and up to overnight.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
Add the bananas, raspberries, and milk to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Add the cocoa powder and chocolate chips. Blend to combine.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin with cooking spray and set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, cinnamon, baking soda, salt, and baking powder.
In a separate medium mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs, yogurt, oil, and sugar.
Add the yogurt mixture, zucchini, and chocolate chips to the flour mixture. Gently fold to combine.
Divide the batter between the prepared muffin tin cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way full.
Bake for 22-25 minutes. Press down gently on the top of one of the muffins to test for doneness. If it springs back up, the muffins are done.
Let the muffins sit in the muffin tin for 5 minutes, then remove and allow to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Serve room temperature or warm.
Add the chocolate chips to a medium mixing bowl and set aside.
Add the garbanzo beans, peanut butter, selected sweetener, and vanilla to a food processor. Pulse to chop and then blend until completely smooth, about 3-5 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to the bowl with the chocolate chips and fold to combine.
Use a 2-tablespoon disher (spring-loaded cookie scoop) to portion the dough out.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
Add the banana to a pint-sized jar or other container with a lid. Mash with a fork.
Add the oats, milk, hemp seeds, selected sweetener, and cinnamon. Stir with the fork to combine.
Place in the refrigerator and chill overnight, or at least 5 hours.
Serve cold, or warm briefly in the microwave before serving.
Place the carrots in a medium or large saucepan and add enough water to just cover the carrots.
Cover the pot with a lid and bring the water to a boil. Then reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the carrots are easily pierced with a fork, about 7-9 minutes.
Drain the carrots into a colander (strainer) and set aside.
Return the pot to the stovetop over medium heat.
Add the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Cook, stirring constantly, until the butter and sugar melt to make a sauce, about 1-2 minutes.
Return the carrots to the pot with the sauce mixture.
Cook, stirring often, until the carrots are coated and the sauce is slightly thickened, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
In a mason jar or single-serving storage container, stir together the oats, milk, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add the fruit and walnuts.
Cover with a lid and refrigerate at least 8 hours, or overnight.
In the morning, grab and go or heat in the microwave for 1-2 minutes if desired.
Add the quinoa and broth to a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cover with a lid and cook until the quinoa is fluffy and tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 30-60 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring often, until they start to break down, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the orange pieces and cook, stirring often, until heated through, about 1-2 minutes.
Transfer the citrus-tomato mixture to a plate or bowl and cover to keep warm. Place the pan back over the heat.
Pat the fish dry with paper towels. Sprinkle the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt and the black pepper on both sides.
Add 1 tablespoon oil to the pan and heat until shimmering.
Place the fish in the pan. Heat until fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 2-4 minutes per side.
Portion the quinoa, fish, and citrus-tomato mixture into four dishes, then serve warm.
Add the quinoa and broth to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
While the quinoa is cooking, in a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, orange zest, orange juice, red wine vinegar, and mustard to make a dressing.
Transfer the cooked quinoa to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine.
Set the quinoa aside to cool for about 5-10 minutes, stirring every 1-2 minutes to allow for quicker cooling.
Add the spinach or arugula, scallions, dried cranberries, parsley, and pecans. Stir to combine.
Add the feta and gently fold to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Add the water and cumin to a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the couscous and stir to combine.
Cover the pot with a lid and remove it from heat. Let sit until the couscous is tender, about 5 minutes.
While the couscous cooks, add the oil and lime juice to a large mixing bowl and whisk together to make a dressing. Add the onion and cilantro. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Fluff the cooked couscous with a fork, then stir in the corn.
Place the lid back on the pot and let sit until the corn is thawed, about 3-5 minutes.
Combine the dressing-onion mixture with the couscous and corn mixture. Add the bell pepper, cucumber, and beans. Toss to combine.
Serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the butter and heat until melted.
Add the celery and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the corn and continue cooking until the celery is tender and the corn is cooked or thawed, about 5 minutes.
Add the salt and pepper. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
Warm a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. Cook until softened, about 5-8 minutes.
Add the oregano, thyme, and black pepper. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth, water, lentils, and tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the lentils are tender, about 20-30 minutes.
Divide the soup between four serving bowls and top each with 1 tablespoon of the parsley.
Serve warm.
Add the quinoa, water, and milk to a small saucepan over high heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Add the cinnamon and vanilla.
Cover the pot with a lid and simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the cranberries and almonds and serve warm, or chill before serving if desired.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a medium mixing bowl, gently toss together the ground turkey, egg, oats, onion, milk, garlic powder, thyme, salt, pepper, and lemon zest (if using).
Use 2-tablespoon cookie scoop (disher) to divide the mixture up and roll into balls. Place the meatballs onto a baking sheet.
Bake the meatballs until they reach an internal temperature of 165°F, about 25-30 minutes.
While the meatballs are cooking, add the glaze ingredients to a small saucepan (pot).

Place the pot over medium-high heat, bring to a rapid simmer, and stir as needed until the glaze is slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Keep warm over low heat until the meatballs are done cooking,
Toss the meatballs with the glaze and serve, or place the glazed meatballs in a slow cooker set to warm and serve from the slow cooker.
Add the bananas, cranberries, orange juice, milk, and ginger (if using) to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture. For a firmer texture, put it in the freezer for 2-3 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.
Pour the milk and orange juice into the pitcher of a blender.
Add the banana, cranberries, carrots, cinnamon, ginger (if using), and ice cubes (if using).
Blend until smooth and fully combined, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve immediately.
Add the cranberries, rosemary, and sugar or agave to a liquid measuring cup.
Using a muddler or the handle of a wooden mixing spoon, smash the cranberries and rosemary until they are broken down and juicy.
Add the soda water and ice. Gently stir to combine.
Pour the cranberry-soda water mixture through a strainer into a drinking glass.
Serve right away, garnishing with cranberries or rosemary if desired.
Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add the oil and butter. Heat until the butter is melted and the oil is shimmering.
Add the celery, potatoes, onion, sage, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine. Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the celery and onion are softened, about 13-15 minutes.
Remove the lid and add the garlic and lemon zest. Cook while stirring for 1 minute.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cook uncovered until the potatoes are tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Working in batches, transfer the broth-vegetable mixture to the pitcher of a blender. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl.
Return the pureed mixture to the pot and stir in the lemon juice. Reheat over the stovetop if needed.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the parsley or celery leaves.
Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook, stirring frequently, until the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and the bread. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the bread is completely saturated and starts to break down, about 3-5 minutes.

Transfer half the tomato mixture to the pitcher of a blender, along with 1 tablespoon of the oil. Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, then transfer the mixture to a large heatproof bowl.
Repeat step 5 with the remaining tomato mixture and 1 tablespoon of oil.
Return all of the blended tomato mixture to the pot. Stir in the broth, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a boil over high heat, then remove the pot from the heat.
Serve warm, topped with the chives or basil as desired.
Add the milk, cottage cheese, parsley, chives, basil, curry powder, and garlic to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot and add just enough water fill the area under the steamer.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-high to maintain a rapid simmer.

Add the potatoes to the steamer basket, cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, and cook until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes. Remove the potatoes from the steamer basket and allow to cool completely.

While the potatoes are cooking, place the eggs in a separate medium saucepan. Add enough water to just cover the eggs. Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and move the pot to a cool burner. Cover the pot with a lid and let sit for 12-15 minutes.
Remove eggs from the pot and place into a bowl of ice-water. Let sit at least 5 minutes, then peel and chop.
In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar or lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Gently fold in the potatoes, eggs, peas, and chives.
Cover the bowl with a lid or plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, then serve cold.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the cauliflower with 2 tablespoons of the oil to coat, then sprinkle with ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Arrange the cauliflower in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet.
Bake until the cauliflower is tender and browned on the edges, about 35-40 minutes, stirring after 20 minutes.
When there is about 10 minutes left on the cauliflower, heat a Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and ¼ teaspoon of the salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30 seconds, then add the broth and cauliflower.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes.
Add the butter, lemon juice, nutmeg, and remaining ¼ teaspoon salt. Blend until smooth using an immersion (handheld) blender.
Garnish each serving with 1 tablespoon of the parsley, chives, or scallion and serve warm.
Add the polenta or grits, water, and salt to a medium saucepan.
