Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, whisking occasionally to break up any lumps, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered until the mixture is thick and pulling away from the sides of the pan, about 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the spinach, bell pepper, butter, and parmesan. Stir to combine.
Continue cooking until heated through, about 2-4 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray or line with parchment paper and set aside.
Pat the cod dry with paper towels.
Crack the egg into a shallow dish and beat lightly with a fork. Set aside.
In another shallow dish, combine the cornmeal, flour, parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, dill, and black pepper. Set aside.
One fillet at a time, dip the cod in the beaten egg and then dip in the cornmeal mixture, covering both sides. Shake off any excess coating and lay the breaded cod on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake until the cod flakes easily with a fork and is golden-brown (minimal internal temperature of 145°F), about 10-15 minutes.
Serve right away.
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly spray a baking sheet with nonstick spray and set aside.
Add the flour to a plate or shallow dish.
In a separate bowl or shallow dish, whisk together the egg, milk, yogurt, and mustard.
Add the cornflakes to a zip-top plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin, meat mallet, or your fist to create crumbs.
Transfer the cornflake crumbs to a medium mixing bowl, along with the black pepper and cayenne. Stir to combine.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels.
Dip the chicken in the flour, coat well, and shake off the excess.
Dip the chicken in the egg mixture, shaking off the excess.
Dip the chicken into the cornflake crumbs, pressing to make the crumbs stick.
Place the chicken on the prepared baking sheet. Bake uncovered until crispy and cooked through (minimum internal temperature of 165°F), about 15-20 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, stir together the peanut butter and maple syrup.
Add the baking soda and salt. Stir to combine.
Add the oats, nuts, dried fruit, and chia seeds (if using). Stir to combine.
Using a tablespoon and filling it until it is heaping over, spoon the dough onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 13 minutes.
Let cool slightly, about 5-10 minutes, before serving.
Heat a medium nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground turkey and cook until no longer pink, about 6-8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles as it cooks.
Add the taco seasoning and water. Stir to combine.
Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Add the lime juice, vinegar, oil, sugar, and cumin to a small jar with a lid. Shake to combine, making a dressing. Set aside.
Divide the lettuce, tomato, cucumber, and corn between two large serving bowls.
Top each bowl with half of the cooked ground turkey.
Sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the cheese and half of the crushed tortilla chips over each bowl. Drizzle each bowl with half of the dressing.
Serve immediately.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Prepare a 12-cup (standard size) muffin tin by spraying each cup with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, toss together the selected cooked vegetables, cheese, and cooked meat (if using)
Divide the vegetable mixture between the muffin tin cups (~2 tablespoons each).
In the same bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, black pepper, and salt.
Divide the egg mixture between the muffin tin cups (~3 tablespoons each).
Bake until the eggs are fully set, about 12-15 minutes.
Let cool completely in the pan, about 7-10 minutes, then carefully remove from the pan. Serve warm.
Add the grated and drained cucumber to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the yogurt, mint, basil, garlic scapes, lemon juice, oil, and salt.
Stir to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
Heat a large pot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, curry powder, ginger, and cayenne. Cook, stirring often, until the onions are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the broth, brown lentils, and pumpkin puree. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the lentils are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil. Coat with nonstick cooking spray, then set aside.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes, stirring often.
Add the curry powder and black pepper. Cook until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes, then transfer to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the salmon, oats, mayonnaise, and lemon or lime juice to the bowl and stir to combine.
Divide the mixture into three portions (⅓ cup each). Shape into patties about ½-inch-thick, then place on the prepared baking sheet.
Spray the patties with nonstick cooking spray, then bake until lightly browned, about 12‐15 minutes. Serve warm.
In a large mixing bowl, make the dressing by whisking together the apple cider vinegar, olive oil, lime juice, sugar, salt, and garlic. Set aside.
Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the edamame to the boiling water and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the frozen corn to the boiling water with the edamame and continue cooking for 1 minute.
Drain the edamame and corn into a colander or strainer.
Add the drained edamame and corn to the bowl with the dressing.
Add the and black beans, tomatoes, and scallions.
Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
Heat a large saucepan or stockpot over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth, cabbage, ginger, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a low simmer.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the cabbage is tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Remove the lid. Use one hand to stir the soup in a steady circle. While the soup is moving, use the other hand to slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs.
Stir in the sesame oil.
Serve warm, garnishing each portion with ½ tablespoon of the green onions.
Fill a medium saucepan with about three inches of water. Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Add the vinegar to the water.
Crack one egg into a small cup and lower the egg into the simmering water, gently pouring it out of the cup. Repeat with the second egg.
Cook the eggs in the water for 3-5 minutes, depending on how soft you want your egg yolk. Remove the cooked eggs gently, one at a time, with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
In a small microwave-safe bowl, add all ingredients for the hollandaise sauce. Microwave on high power (default setting) until smooth and frothy, about 60 seconds, stopping to whisk every 15 seconds.
Toast the English muffin.
Place the Canadian bacon on a small microwave-safe plate and heat on high power (default setting) for 30 seconds.
Top each English muffin half with one slice of the bacon, one poached egg, and half of the sauce. Serve right away.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, mustard, oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add fennel, carrot, and parsley. Toss to combine.
(Optional) Chill for 1 hour for best flavor.
Serve cold.
Place a steamer basket inside a large saucepan or stockpot.
Add water until it reaches just below the bottom of the steamer basket. Set over high heat and bring to a simmer.
While the water in the pot is heating, fill a large mixing bowl halfway with ice and water. Set near the stovetop.
Add the green beans to the steamer basket inside the pot.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook until the green beans are tender but still crisp, about 4-6 minutes.

Use an oven mitt or hot pad to carefully remove the steamer basket from the pot. Transfer the green beans to the bowl of ice water, then remove and place on paper towels to dry. Pat dry to speed up the process if needed.
Drain and wipe the bowl dry with paper towels. Add the dressing ingredients and whisk to combine.
Add the green beans, chives, almonds, cranberries or cherries, and parmesan. Toss to combine with the dressing.
Serve, warming or chilling before serving desired.
In a medium bowl, make a salsa by stirring together the strawberries, onion, garlic, cilantro, jalapeño, lime juice, salt, and ⅛ teaspoon of the black pepper. Set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the cumin, paprika, and the remaining ⅛ teaspoon of black pepper. Set aside.
Pat the pollock dry with paper towels.
Brush the pollock with the olive oil, then sprinkle the seasoning mixture over both sides.
Coat the inside of a medium nonstick skillet with cooking spray and place over medium heat.
When the pan is hot, place the pollock in the pan and cook until a crust is formed and the fish lifts easy from the pan, about 2-4 minutes.
Flip the pollock over and continue cooking until cooked through (flakes easily with a fork, internal temperature of 145°F), about 3-5 minutes. Remove from the pan and set aside.
Heat the tortillas in the pan or in the microwave until warm.
Break the fish into bite-sized pieces. Serve on the warmed tortillas, topped with the strawberry salsa and any other desired garnishes.
In a small bowl, combine 1 tablespoon of the taco seasoning, 1 tablespoon of the lime juice, and 1 tablespoon of the oil. Coat the fish fillets with the mixture.
In a separate small bowl, combine the remaining 1 tablespoon of taco seasoning with the yogurt, mayonnaise, and 1 tablespoon of the lime juice. Set aside.

In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons lime juice, 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, cilantro, honey or sugar, black pepper, and salt. Add the shredded cabbage and toss to coat. Set aside.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the fish and cook until it is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 3-6 minutes per side. Remove the fish from the pan and let it rest for 1-2 minutes.
Break the fish into bite-sized pieces, then divide the pieces of fish and the dressed cabbage over the warmed tortillas.
Serve warm, drizzling with the yogurt mixture to taste.
Spray the inside of a microwave‐safe mug with nonstick cooking spray. Set aside.
Crack the egg into a small bowl, then gently whisk the yolk and white together with a fork.
Add the flax meal, cinnamon, baking powder, and stevia. Stir with the fork until well combined, then gently stir in the blueberries.
Pour the mixture into the prepared mug, then microwave on high power (default setting) until fully set but not dry, about 1½-2 minutes.
Let cool in the mug for 2-5 minutes, then turn the mug over and gently shake to remove the muffin.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Coat the inside of an 8x8-inch baking pan with cooking spray and set aside.
Add the beans to the pitcher of a food processor or blender, and pulse until broken down, about 10-15 pulses.
Scrape down the sides and add the eggs. Pulse until well-combined, about 10-15 pulses.
Add the sugar, cocoa powder, milk, vinegar, oil, baking powder, baking soda, coffee, and salt. Pulse or blend on low speed until fully combined.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl and stir in ½ cup of the chocolate.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking pan, spreading it to the edges.
Sprinkle the top with the remaining ¼ cup of chocolate.
Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean with no batter or crumbs, about 25-30 minutes.
Let cool in the pan for at least 10 minutes.
Cut the brownies into 16 squares and serve.

recipes.title: Fresh Corn and Roasted Red Pepper Salad

steps.text: Place one ear of corn, with the husk on, in the microwave and cook on high (default power) for 2 minutes. Carefully remove from the microwave and set aside. Repeat with the remaining ears of corn.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, ⅓ cup of the lemon juice, 1½ teaspoons of the lemon zest, ginger, honey, turmeric, and salt.
Add the cabbage, roasted peppers, peaches, tomatoes, and basil. Toss to combine and set aside.
When the corn is cool enough to handle, remove the husks but leave stalks on. Cut a small slice off the tip of each ear to create a flat surface.
Place a small bowl upside-down inside a larger bowl.
Working one ear at a time, hold the stalk of an ear of corn and place the tip on top of the small bowl. Cutting lengthwise from the stalk to the tip, cut the kernels off the ear of corn.
Mix the corn kernels into cabbage-pepper mixture.
Serve, topping each serving with a quarter of the avocado and 1 tablespoon of the feta.

recipes.title: Fresh Green Salad with Lemony Dressing

steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, water, mustard, honey, black pepper, and salt (if using) to make a dressing. Set aside.
Wash and dry the salad greens and place them in a large mixing or serving bowl.
Add the tomatoes, cucumber, and carrots.
Add the dressing and toss to coat.
Serve immediately.
Put the garlic cloves in a food processor and pulse or blend until fully minced, about 30 seconds.
Add the parsley and oregano and pulse until fully chopped, about 30-60 seconds, scraping down the sides as needed.
Add the vinegar, salt, crushed red pepper (if using), and black pepper. Pulse to combine, about 30 seconds.
Transfer the mixture to a serving bowl or storage container.
Pour the oil over the top and gently stir to combine. Set aside for 15-20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve at room temperature, or place in the refrigerator until needed.
Add the basil and/or parsley, nuts or seeds, parmesan, oil, lemon juice, garlic, and salt to the bowl of a food processor or blender.
Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
In a quart-size mason jar or other 4-cup storage container, stir together the oats, milk, chia seeds, and cinnamon.
Add the fruit and nuts.
Cover with a lid and refrigerate overnight, or at least 8 hours.
Serve cold, or heat in the microwave for 1-2 minutes and serve warm.
Fill a large pot or saucepan halfway full with water. Set over high heat and bring to a boil.
Meanwhile, prepare a large bowl with ice water and make an X cut with a paring knife on the bottom of each tomato.
Carefully drop the tomatoes into the boiling water and cook for 15 seconds, then remove and transfer to the ice water.
Let tomatoes cool until able to handle, about 1 minute, then remove from the ice water and pat dry.
Peel and seed the tomatoes. To seed the tomatoes, place them in a fine mesh strainer set over a large mixing bowl. Press as much of the juice and pulp through as possible.
Transfer the collected juice and pulp to a liquid measuring cup. Add canned tomato juice to bring the total to 1 cup.
Transfer the tomatoes and juice back to the bowl. Add the cucumber, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño, garlic, lime juice, vinegar, soy sauce or tamari, cumin, salt, and black pepper. Stir to combine.
Transfer 1½ cups of the mixture to a blender and add the olive oil. Blend on high speed until smooth and creamy, about 20-30 seconds.
Return the pureed mixture to the bowl and stir to combine.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, up to overnight.
Serve cold, garnishing with the basil.

recipes.title: Garlic Avocado Toast with Fried Egg

steps.text: Place the bread slices in a toaster, under a broiler, or in a skillet over medium heat. Toast to the desired level of doneness.
Rub the cut side of one of the garlic clove halves on one side of each slice of toasted bread.

Use a spoon to scoop the flesh of the avocado out into a small bowl. Add the lime juice and mash together with a fork. Divide the mixture over the slices of toasted bread and spread to cover one side of each slice. Set aside.
Spray a small or medium skillet with cooking spray and place over medium heat. When the pan is hot, crack the eggs in the pan and cook to desired doneness.
Slide one of the eggs from the skillet onto the top of each slice of avocado toast.
Top each egg with half of the feta, parsley, and black pepper. Serve right away.
Cut the potatoes in half lengthwise, then cut each of the halves lengthwise again to create quarters. Cut the potatoes crosswise into ½-inch-thick slices.
Add the potatoes to a large pot. Add just enough cold water to cover them.
Cover the pot with a lid and bring the water to a boil over high heat. When the water begins to boil, remove the lid and bring the heat down to a simmer.
Cook the potatoes until they are easily crushed with tongs, about 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the half-and-half, garlic, lemon juice or vinegar, and salt to a small saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat.
Drain the potatoes, then return them to the pot and place the pot back over the heat.
Add the warm half-and-half mixture to the potatoes.
Mash the potatoes until you are happy with the texture. If you are using red potatoes, keep in mind that they will not get completely smooth with mashing.
Serve warm, topping as desired.

recipes.title: Gazpacho Dip with Garlic Pita Chips

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Cut each pita round into 6 wedges.
Separate each wedge horizontally into 2 pieces.
Arrange the pita wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Lightly coat the pita wedges with nonstick spray and sprinkle with garlic powder and salt.
Bake until the wedges curl at the edges and begin to brown, about 6-8 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine the tomato, celery, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, red wine vinegar, black pepper, and fresh herbs. Stir to combine.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Serve the dip cold with the pita chips.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Spray an 8x8-inch baking pan lightly with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the blueberries and ginger. Spread the mixture into the bottom of the prepared baking pan.
In a separate small mixing bowl, add the oats, flour, sugar, butter, and cinnamon. Mix with a fork or pastry blender until the mixture is combined and crumbly.
Sprinkle the oat mixture over the blueberry mixture.
Place the baking dish in the preheated oven and cook until the oat topping is lightly browned and crispy, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and let cool at room temperature for at least 20 minutes before serving.
In a large bowl, whisk together the lime zest, lime juice, and olive oil. Set aside.
Combine the rinsed quinoa with the water in a saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil, then cover with a lid and reduce to a simmer.
Cook until all liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Set the cooked quinoa aside to cool, about 10-15 minutes.
In a large bowl, toss the cooled quinoa, grapes, cucumbers, spinach, scallions, and mint together with the dressing.
Season with pepper to taste.
Gently fold in the avocado.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.

recipes.title: Greek Yogurt with Warm Berry Sauce

steps.text: Combine the frozen berries and lime juice in a small saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until a sauce forms and thickens, about 10-12 minutes.
Divide the yogurt into four serving bowls.
Top each serving of yogurt with a quarter of the sauce (about ⅓ cup).
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the almonds and cook until toasted, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the butter and cook, stirring often, until melted and golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the almond mixture to a small bowl.
Add the lemon juice and stir to combine, then set aside.
Return the pan to the stovetop over medium heat.
Add the green beans, water, and salt.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the green beans are almost tender, about 6-8 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook until the green beans are tender and the liquid is evaporated, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the almond mixture. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the oil and 2 tablespoons of the lime juice.
Add the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and oregano. Stir to combine.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towels, then add to the bowl and toss to coat. Set aside.
Preheat the grill to medium-high (about 400°F) or a grill pan on the stovetop over medium-high heat.
When the grill or grill pan is hot, add the chicken and cook through (internal temperature of 165°F), about 4-7 minutes on each side.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and let rest for 5-7 minutes, then cut into bite-sized strips or cubes.
While the chicken rests, in a small bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, cilantro, salt, black pepper, and remaining 2 tablespoons of lime juice to make a dressing.
Gather four serving bowls and add 2 cups of the lettuce, ¼ cup of the tomato, and ¼ cup of the corn to each .
Top each bowl with a quarter of each of the following: black beans (~⅓ cup each), avocado (~¼ cup each), onion (~¼ cup each), and dressing (~2 tablespoons each).
Divide the chicken between the bowls
Serve right away.

recipes.title: Hearty Bell Pepper and Turkey Skillet

steps.text: Heat a large heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and sauté until soft and transparent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the ground turkey and bell pepper. Continue to sauté until the bell peppers are soft and the turkey is fully cooked, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes and their juice, rice, basil, oregano, broth, tomato sauce, and Worcestershire sauce. Stir to combine.
Place the lid on the skillet. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cook until the rice is tender and most of the liquid has been absorbed, about for 10-15 minutes. Add additional broth or water if needed to cook the rice.
Serve warm.
Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the ground turkey and onion. Cook, stirring often, until the turkey is no longer pink and the onion is softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chili powder, pumpkin pie spice, cumin, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth, diced tomatoes with their juice, pumpkin puree, kidney beans, black beans, garbanzo beans, green chiles, and apple cider vinegar. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 35-45 minutes.

Serve warm, topping as desired. NOTE: To make the recipe in a slow cooker, add the ingredients and stir to combine. Cover the slow cooker with the lid, then set the slow cooker to cook on low for 8-12 hours (or on high for 4-6 hours).
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Coat a 12-cup muffin pan with nonstick spray. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, whole-wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice or cinnamon.
In a separate large mixing bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, oil, and eggs. Add the pumpkin puree, milk, and vanilla extract. Whisk to combine.
Gradually add the flour mixture to the pumpkin mixture, stirring gently just until combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared muffin pan, filling each cup all the way to the top.
Bake until a toothpick comes out clean when inserted into the center of the muffins, about 18-22 minutes.
Let cool in the muffin pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cooling rack. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Heat a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, celery, carrots, and jalapeño.
Sauté until the onions are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Stir in the lentils, broth, tomatoes with their juice, cumin, and ground black pepper.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cover with a lid and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the spinach. Cook until the spinach is thawed and the soup is warmed through.
Serve warm.
In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, honey, lime juice, and ginger to make a sauce. Set aside.

Chop and slice the selected vegetables. Arrange in order of cooking time, from longest (hard/tough vegetables; onion, carrots, broccoli) to shortest (soft vegetables; snap peas, asparagus, zucchini). If using frozen vegetables, skip this step and add all the vegetables at the beginning of cooking.
Prepare the selected protein (small dice or thin slice, unless using shrimp or eggs).
Heat a large skillet, sauté pan, or wok over high heat.
Add the oil and the longest-cooking vegetables and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the protein and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes.
Add the shortest-cooking vegetables and cook, stirring constantly, for 4 minutes.
Add the sauce and cashews or peanuts (if using). Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Divide the rice or quinoa between four bowls and divide the vegetable-protein mixture between the bowls. Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Slice the bread diagonally into 12 slices, about ½-inch-thick. Place the bread slices on a baking sheet and brush with the olive oil.
Bake until toasted, about 5 minutes, flipping about halfway through the cooking time.
Add the fruit, vinegar or lemon juice, honey, salt, and black pepper to a small mixing bowl. Toss to combine.
Divide the fruit mixture, between the bread slices (~1 tablespoon each). Top each slice 1 teaspoon of the cheese, then serve.
Drain the chickpeas. Reserve the canning liquid and set aside.
Put the chickpeas in a food processor or blender.
Add the garlic, lemon juice, tahini, oil, black pepper, salt, and half of the reserved chickpea canning liquid (about ⅓ cup).
Puree the until very smooth, about 2-3 minutes, adding additional canning liquid as necessary to produce a thick dip.
Add additional lemon juice to taste, if desired.
Transfer to a serving dish (or a storage container if you’re not eating it right away). Garnish with paprika.
Serve right away, or store in an air-tight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Can be frozen if desired.
Add the cranberries, orange zest, orange juice, honey, water, cinnamon, cloves, and salt to medium saucepan.
Set the saucepan over high heat and bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium.
Continue cooking, stirring often, until the cranberries break down. The sauce should thicken and reduce to about 2 cups.
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little extra water to reach the desired consistency. Note that the sauce will continue to thicken as it cools.
Serve warm, or chill before serving.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Combine the sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl. Set aside.
Brush both sides of each tortilla lightly with the oil.
Cut each tortilla into wedges; 8 wedges for whole-wheat tortillas, 4 wedges for corn tortillas.
Lightly sprinkle both sides of the tortilla wedges with the cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Place the tortilla wedges in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Place in the oven and cook until the tortilla wedges are golden-brown and crispy, about 7-10 minutes, flipping them over about halfway through the cooking time.
Serve immediately, or store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
Add the milk, heavy cream, and salt to a large saucepan or stockpot. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn off the heat.
Add the vinegar or lemon juice and stir to combine.
Let sit until large curds separate from the liquid (whey), about 7-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, line a colander or strainer with two layers of damp paper towels and place over the mouth of a large bowl.
Carefully pour or ladle the milk mixture into the colander and strainer. Let drain to the desired consistency, about 30-40 minutes.
Use right away, or refrigerate for up to 7 days. Discard the liquid (whey) or use it in place of buttermilk in other recipes.
Spread the hummus over the tortilla.
Layer the tortilla with the salad greens, onion, cucumber, tomato, and carrots.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette.
Fold the sides of the tortilla over towards the center, then roll up tightly.
Serve cold.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is softened and slightly brown, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chile peppers, coriander, turmeric, chili powder, and black pepper. Cook, stirring often, for 3-4 minutes.
Add the cauliflower florets. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes.
Add the water and cover the pan with a lid.
Cook until the cauliflower is fork-tender, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the peas and continue cooking until warmed through, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm, with a lime wedge to squeeze on juice as desired.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, combine the garlic powder, coriander, cumin, salt, and cayenne with a fork. Toss the chicken breasts in the spice mixture.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chicken, sprinkling any of the remaining seasoning mixture on top, and sear until golden-brown, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Add the ginger, coconut milk, and tomatoes with their juice. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pan with a lid.
Heat until the chicken is cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the spinach and cover the pan with the lid. Let cook until the spinach is wilted, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice.
Layer into six bowls with the rice on the bottom, then the spinach, sauce, and chicken. Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
Heat a skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the bell pepper, onion, and salt. Cook until the bell pepper and onion are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the pepper-onion mixture to a large mixing bowl.
Add the ground beef, carrot, ketchup, egg, breadcrumbs, tomato paste, mustard, basil, oregano, thyme, garlic powder, and black pepper and mix until well combined.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet and shape the mixture into a loaf.
Bake until the meatloaf is firm and reaches an internal temperature of 160°F, about 35-45 minutes.
Cover the meatloaf loosely with foil and let it rest for 5-10 minutes, then cut it into six slices. Serve warm.
Heat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, garlic, Italian seasoning, cayenne, and salt.
Sauté until the onion is softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, bell pepper, zucchini, beans, corn, and broth.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook uncovered until the vegetables are tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Serve warm.
Warm a large saucepan or pot over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and cook until softened and starting to brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Add the Italian seasoning, garlic, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth and the orzo.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn the heat down to maintain a simmer.
Slice open the sausage casing and pinch off a small amount of the meat (about the size of a marble). Drop the pieces of meat directly into the simmering broth.
Continue simmering until the orzo is tender and the meatballs are cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach and lemon juice. Stir to combine.
Serve warm.
Trim the ends of the cucumber and cut each cucumber crosswise into thirds, then cut in half lengthwise.
Place the cucumbers in a large plastic zip-top bag and seal the bag. Place the bag on a hard, durable surface such as a clean cutting board.
Use a skillet or a sauté pan to smash the cucumbers in the bag until they start to split lengthwise.
Tear or cut the cucumbers into bite-sized pieces, then add them to a colander placed inside a bowl or over the sink.
Sprinkle the cucumbers with the salt and toss to combine.
Let the cucumbers sit to remove their excess liquid, at least 15 minutes and up to 30 minutes.

While the cucumbers sit, add the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and red pepper flakes (if using) to a medium mixing bowl. Stir together until the sugar has dissolved to make a dressing, about 1 minute.
Add the cucumbers to the bowl with the dressing and toss to combine. Discard the liquid drained from the cucumber.
Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
In a medium mixing bowl, whisk together the lime juice, oil, and honey.
Add the jicama, carrot, and cilantro. Toss to combine and coat with the dressing.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
In a large mixing or serving bowl, add 2 tablespoons of lemon juice, oil, honey or maple syrup, mustard, salt, and black pepper and whisk well to create a dressing. Set aside.
Cut the fennel bulb into quarters lengthwise and remove the core from each piece. Cut each quarter into thin slices, with a knife or a slicing tool (e.g. box grater, mandoline).
In a medium mixing bowl, toss the shaved fennel with the remaining 2 tablespoons of lemon juice. Set aside.
Remove the large stems from the kale and cut or tear into bite-sized pieces. Add to the bowl with the dressing. Using clean hands, toss and massage the kale with the dressing.
Cut the pear in half lengthwise and scrape out the core with the tip of a spoon. Cut each half lengthwise into thin slices.
Add the pear and fennel to the bowl with the kale and toss to combine.
Serve, topping each serving with 2 tablespoons of the blue cheese and 2 tablespoons of the walnuts.
Preheat the oven to 300°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
Wash the kale and pat dry. Remove the leaves from the stems, discarding the stems. Place the leaves in a large mixing bowl.
Add the oil and rub onto the surface of the kale leaves.
Add the nutritional yeast (if using), selected spice(s), and salt. Toss to combine.
Spread the kale into a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake until crispy, about 20-25 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through the cooking time.
Let cool, then serve at room temperature.
In a small bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, cucumber, mint, and 1 teaspoon of the lemon juice. Set aside.
In a separate small mixing bowl, whisk together the broth, vinegar, oil, garlic, rosemary, salt, black pepper, and the remaining lemon juice to make a marinade.
Transfer the marinade mixture to a large plastic ziptop bag. Set the bag inside the bowl that held the marinade.
Add the cubed lamb to the marinade and toss to coat.
Seal the bag, squeezing out the excess air, and refrigerate in the bowl for at least 20 minutes, up to overnight.
Gather 12 skewers. If using wooden or bamboo skewers, soak them in warm water for at least 15 minutes to prevent the ends from burning and turning black.
While the skewers are soaking, heat up the grill to medium heat or the broiler to high heat. If the broiler is in the oven, set an oven rack to the middle position.
While the broiler or grill is heating, thread the marinated lamb cubes, zucchini, bell pepper, and onion onto the skewers.
Cook on the grill or under the broiler (on the middle rack if in the oven) for 15-20 minutes, turning every 4-5 minutes, until cooked through (internal temperature of 145°F).
Drizzle with yogurt mixture, then serve warm.
Place a large pot over medium heat on the stovetop.
Add the oil and onion. Cook, stirring often, until the onion is translucent, about 5-8 minutes.
Add the ground turkey, oregano, and garlic. Cook until the turkey is almost completely cooked, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the broth, tomatoes, and tomato sauce.
Turn the heat up to high and bring to a boil.
Add the lasagna noodles and continue cooking at a boil until they are tender but still a little chewy (al dente), about 10-12 minutes.
Divide the soup between six serving bowls and top each with 2 tablespoons of the ricotta.
Serve warm.

In a parfait glass or bowl, layer the following ingredients in this order: ⅓ cup of the Greek yogurt, ½ tablespoon of the honey, all of the cranberry sauce, 2 tablespoons of the granola, 1 teaspoon of the chia seeds or hemp seeds, and 1 teaspoon of the ground flax.
Repeat with a second layer, with the remaining ⅓ cup Greek yogurt, ½ tablespoon honey, 2 tablespoons granola, 1 teaspoon chia seeds or hemp seeds, and 1 teaspoon ground flax.
Serve immediately.
In a small bowl, add the Greek yogurt and cranberry sauce. Stir to combine, then set aside.
Lay the warmed tortilla on a clean flat surface, such as a cutting board. Spread the yogurt mixture evenly over the tortilla, leaving about a 1-inch border on all sides.
Layer the turkey, avocado, lettuce, carrot, tomato, green onion, and black pepper onto the bottom half of the tortilla, still leaving a 1-inch border.
Roll up the tortilla into a wrap by folding the sides in toward the center, then rolling the bottom up toward the top.
(Optional) Heat the wrap under the broiler until lightly toasted, about 2-3 minutes on each side.
Cut the wrap in half and serve.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Place the broccoli in the pan and sauté until bright green, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the water and sauté until fork-tender, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the lemon juice, parmesan, and black pepper to the broccoli. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
Heat a medium or large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the uncooked orzo pasta. Cook, stirring often, until golden and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the garlic, zucchini, and carrot. Cook, stirring often, for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and lemon zest. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Cook until the liquid has been absorbed and orzo is al dente (tender, yet still a little chewy), about 10 minutes.
Stir in the thyme.
Serve warm, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of parmesan cheese.

recipes.title: Lemony Pan-Seared Fish with Wilted Kale

steps.text: Cut the lemon in half lengthwise. Juice one of the halves into a small bowl. Cut the other half into four wedges. Set the lemon juice and lemon wedges aside.
On a clean plate or other surface (e.g. cutting board), pat the fish dry with paper towels, then season it evenly on both sides with the seasoning blend and chopped dill.
Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ½ tablespoon of the oil to the pan.
Add the fish and cook on the first side until browned, about 2-4 minutes.
Turn the fish over and heat until cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 4-6 minutes.
Transfer the fish to a clean plate and cover with foil.
Add the remaining ½ tablespoon of oil to the pan.
Add the kale and cook until wilted, about 2-4 minutes.
Add the lemon juice and stir to combine.
Transfer the kale to the plate with the fish and serve warm, squeezing on additional lemon juice as desired.
Melt the butter in a small skillet over low heat. Keep it in the pan to stay warm.
Fill a medium saucepan three-quarters full with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Find a heat-resistant metal mixing bowl that fits in the mouth of the saucepan without touching the water. With the bowl off the heat, add and whisk together the eggs, lemon juice, and salt.
Add ⅓ cup water to a microwave-safe bowl or liquid measuring cup. Microwave until very hot, about 1 minute.

Place the heat-resistant metal bowl on the mouth of the saucepan over the simmering water to make a double boiler. The bowl shouldn’t touch the water. If it does, pour out small amounts of the water until it does not.
Whisk constantly, adding the ⅓ cup hot water in a slow but steady stream, until the eggs have thickened to a ribbony, lemon-yellow creamy, and uniform texture.
Turn off the heat and add the butter in a slow but steady stream, whisking constantly.
Add the cayenne and serve warm.
Crack the eggs into a small bowl. Add the milk and black pepper. Whisk with fork until combined, then set aside.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion, mushrooms, and bell pepper. Cook, stirring often, until tender and lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Transfer the vegetable mixture to a plate and set aside.
Spray the pan with nonstick spray and return the pan to the stovetop. Reduce the heat to medium-low.
Add the egg mixture to the pan and cover the pan with a lid.
Allow the eggs to cook, without stirring, until firm but still moist, about 2-4 minutes.
Remove the lid and sprinkle the vegetable mixture and cheese over one half of the cooked eggs.
Fold the other half of eggs over the vegetables and cheese.
Turn off the heat and cover the pan with the lid until the cheese is melted, about 2-3 minutes, then serve warm.
Gather four microwave-safe food storage containers with lids.
Combine the cooked whole grain with the green chiles. Divide this mixture evenly among the four containers.
Divide the beans evenly among the four containers.
Add 1 cup of the chicken and ¼ of the cup corn to each of the four containers.
Add 1 cup of the lettuce or salad greens to each container.
Top each container with 2 tablespoons salsa, 2 tablespoons Greek yogurt, and 2 tablespoons scallions.
Cover the containers with lids and store in refrigerator until ready to eat, up to 3 days.
When ready to eat, microwave each container on high power (default setting) until hot, about 1-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.
In large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon.
Add the oats and pecans. Toss gently until completely coated with the oil-maple syrup mixture.
Transfer the mixture onto the prepared baking and spread into an even layer.
Bake until golden-brown and crispy, about 20-25 minutes, stirring the mixture every 7-10 minutes.
Remove from oven and place on a wire cooling rack or other heat-safe surface.
When completely cooled, use as desired or transfer to an airtight storage container for up to 2 months.
To a medium mixing bowl or a jar with a lid, add the oil, vinegar, lemon juice, garlic powder, oregano, basil, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.
Whisk together the oil-vinegar mixture in the bowl or place the lid on the jar and shake, mixing until combined to make a marinade.
Place the selected vegetables in a large bowl.
Pour the marinade over the vegetables and toss until evenly coated.
Set the vegetables in the refrigerator to marinate, at least 30 minutes and up to overnight.
Serve cold, or cook as desired and serve warm.
Place the potatoes and fresh cauliflower (if using frozen, see step 2) in a medium saucepan. Add water to cover and bring to a boil.

Reduce the heat to low and simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender and the cauliflower is very soft (overcooked), about 15 minutes. (If using frozen cauliflower, add after the potatoes have been boiling for 5 minutes. Bring back to a boil and continue cooking for the additional 10 minutes.)
Drain the potatoes and cauliflower into a strainer.
Transfer the cauliflower to a blender or food processor, along with the garlic, milk, butter, salt, and pepper. Puree until smooth.
Add the potatoes and pureed cauliflower mixture back to the pan. Mash together until smooth and combined.
Stir in the parsley (if using) and serve warm.
Add the kale to a large mixing or serving bowl.
Add 4 tablespoons (¼ cup) of the lemon juice, 2 tablespoons of the oil, and the salt.
Massage the kale until it wilts down in size by about half and it feels more tender, about 1-2 minutes, making sure each leaf is coated with the lemon juice-oil mixture. Set aside.
In a small bowl, make a dressing by whisking together the honey, salt, black pepper, the remaining 2 tablespoons lemon juice, and the remaining 1 tablespoon oil.
Pour the dressing over the kale, along with the sunflower seeds and tomatoes. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving.
In a small bowl, whisk together the dressing ingredients and set aside.
Heat a small pan over medium-low heat.
Add the almonds to the pan and toast until light brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Transfer the almonds to a medium mixing bowl.
Add the cooked and chilled barley, chickpeas, roasted red peppers, and dates to the mixing bowl with the almonds. Stir to combine.
Pour the dressing over the barley mixture, whisking to recombine if needed. Toss to coat.
Gently fold in the feta cheese.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the lemon juice or vinegar, oil, oregano, and red pepper flakes to make a dressing.
Add the onion and garlic. Stir to combine, then let sit for at least 10 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, and bell pepper. Toss to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired.
Add the quinoa and water to a medium saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to maintain a simmer. Cook until the quinoa is tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat. Fluff the cooked quinoa with a fork and let sit to cool. You can speed up this process by spreading it on a baking sheet and putting it in the refrigerator.
In a medium mixing bowl, make the dressing by whisking together the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, and mustard.
Add the cooked and cooled quinoa, along with the cucumber, red peppers or tomatoes, olives, parsley, and feta. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately, or chill before serving if desired, up to 5 days.
Place the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, and salt in a 12-ounce microwave-safe ceramic mug. Whisk with a fork.
Add the milk, oil, and vanilla. Whisk again with the fork until smooth.
Stir in the chocolate chips.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Microwave for another 30 seconds if needed, but be careful not to overcook or the cake will be dry.
Let sit to cool slightly and firm up, about 2-3 minutes.
Serve warm.
Add the berries, cornstarch, and salt to a microwave-safe bowl.
Toss to combine until the cornstarch is no longer white.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 2 minutes.
Stir, then continue microwaving on high power (default setting) until slightly thickened and warmed through, about 2-3 minutes more.
Let cool until not too hot to taste, about 2-4 minutes, then add the sugar or honey (if using). Stir to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving if desired.
Coat the inside of a large microwave-safe mug or bowl with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the pepper and onion blend and sausage. Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Use a paper towel to carefully soak up any liquid.
Add the English muffin pieces and cheese. Stir to combine, then set aside.
In a separate small bowl, use a fork to whisk together the eggs, milk, and black pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over English muffin mixture, then let sit for 1-2 minutes to soak.
Microwave on high power (default setting) until the eggs are no longer runny, about 2-3 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm.
Add the bell peppers and onion to an 8x8-inch or 9x9-inch microwave-safe glass baking dish (or other 8-10 cup microwave-safe dish) that has a lid.
Add the oil and 2 tablespoons of the seasoning. Toss to coat the vegetables.
Coat the chicken with the remaining 2 tablespoons of seasoning, then place on top of the vegetables.
Cover dish with the lid and microwave on high power (default setting) until the chicken is cooked through (internal temperature of 165°F) and the vegetables are tender, about 7-10 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then slice the chicken and toss with the vegetable mixture.
Divide the chicken-vegetable mixture between the tortillas (~⅔ cup each). Serve warm, adding toppings as desired.
Add the butter to a microwave-safe mug or bowl.
Place in the microwave and cook on high (default power) until melted, about 15-30 seconds. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, tear the bread into bite-sized pieces. Set aside.
When the butter has cooled, add the milk, egg, brown sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla to the mug or bowl. Whisk with a fork to combine.
Add the pieces of bread, stirring to coat and pressing them down into the milk-egg mixture. Let sit for 1-2 minutes to soak.
Place in the microwave on top of a plate or paper towel. Cook on high (default power) until the liquid is fully set, about 1½-2 minutes.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm, topping as desired.
Spray the inside of a microwave-safe mug or bowl with nonstick cooking spray.
Add the eggs, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper. Whisk with a fork to combine.
Add the turkey, bell pepper, and spinach or broccoli. Stir to combine.
Microwave on high power (default setting) in 1-minute increments until the eggs are fully set. This will take about 2-3 minutes in total.
Let sit for 2 minutes, then serve warm.

recipes.title: Microwave Vegetable Omelet in a Mug

steps.text: Spray the inside of a microwave-safe mug with nonstick cooking spray. Add the selected vegetable(s) and water.
Microwave on high power (default setting) until the vegetables are tender, about ½-3 minutes depending on the type of vegetable(s).
Use a paper towel to carefully soak up any liquid in the mug.
Add the eggs and cheese, whisking with a fork to combine. Microwave on high power (default setting) for 1 minute.
Stir gently with the fork, then continue microwaving until the eggs are just set but still moist, about 15-45 seconds.
Let cool slightly, then serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
In a mixing bowl, add the pureed pumpkin, oil, yogurt, eggs, sugar, and vanilla. Stir to combine.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice. Whisk to combine.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients. Stir until combined.
Add the chocolate chips. Stir to combine.
Spoon the batter into a greased mini muffin tin, filling each cup about ¾ of the way full.
Bake for 15 minutes. To check if they are done, press lightly on each muffin. The muffin should spring back up when pressed.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.

In a medium mixing bowl, add the ground turkey, oats, carrots, spinach, parmesan cheese, egg, garlic powder, Italian seasoning or oregano, salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and 3 tablespoons of the tomato sauce or ketchup. Gently knead the mixture together until well-combined.
Spray 8 regular-sized muffin tin cups with nonstick spray.
Fill each prepared muffin tin cup with the meatloaf mixture. If needed, prepare an additional 1-2 cups for any extra meatloaf mixture.
In a small bowl, stir together the remaining 3 tablespoons of tomato sauce or ketchup with the brown sugar. Spread ½ tablespoon of this mixture over each meatloaf.
Bake until the center reaches 165°F, about 25-30 minutes.

Cool slightly, then remove from the muffin tins and serve warm. Refrigerate for up to 4 days, freeze for up to 3 months. To serve, thaw in the refrigerator and heat in the microwave or oven to an internal temperature of 165°F.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place the naan bread on a cutting board.
Add the sauce and spread evenly over the bread.
Sprinkle evenly with the cheese and vegetables.
Transfer the naan bread with toppings to the oven, placing it directly on the oven rack.
Bake until the cheese is melted, about 7-9 minutes.
Carefully remove the pizza from the oven and transfer to the cutting board. Let cool for 5 minutes.
Cut in half with a pizza cutter or large knife.
Serve warm.
Add the oats, almond meal, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and clove to a food processor. Pulse until the mixture is a fine texture like flour.
Add the dates, honey, and vanilla. Pulse until the mixture comes together.
Use a small scoop or spoon (about a tablespoon) to portion the mixture out, then roll the mixture into balls.
Serve right away, or chill before serving.
In a small bowl, stir together the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and cinnamon to form a crumbly mixture.
Gather four small jars or other serving containers and divide the mixture between them, about 1 tablespoon in each. Press down to form a crust.

In a medium mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to beat together the Greek yogurt, cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla. Continue to beat until the mixture is completely smooth and resembles a very thick whipped cream.
Divide the yogurt-cream cheese mixture between the jars.
Place in the refrigerator to chill, at least 1 hour.
Serve cold.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the oats, coconut, flax meal, pepitas, nut or seed butter, honey, chia seeds or hemp hearts, vanilla, and cinnamon.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator to chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the mixture into 1-inch balls. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 3 months.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oats and pecans. Cook until lightly browned and fragrant, about 6-8 minutes, stirring often.
Transfer the oats and pecans to a food processor, along with the brown sugar, butter, and ½ teaspoon of the cinnamon.
Pulse to chop, then continue blending until the mixture looks like wet sand, about 2-3 minutes. Transfer the mixture to a bowl or plate and set aside.

In the food processor, add the cream cheese, pumpkin puree, yogurt, sugar, and remaining 1½ teaspoons cinnamon. Blend until completely smooth and airy, about 3-5 minutes, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.

Gather eight small (~½-cup) jars, drinking glasses, bowls, or storage containers. Add 1 tablespoon of the oat mixture to each and press down firmly to make a crust. Divide the cream cheese mixture over the crusts (~⅓ cup each), followed by the remaining oat mixture (~½ teaspoon each).
Cover the containers with lids or plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, then serve cold.
Heat a large skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the okra and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, oregano, Cajun seasoning, and lemon juice.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pan with a lid and cook until the okra is tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 300°F
In a large bowl, combine the oats, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, shredded coconut, maple syrup or brown sugar, olive oil, cinnamon or pumpkin pie spice, and salt.
Divide the mixture between 2 rimmed baking sheets and spread in an even layer.
Bake until golden-brown and crispy, about 30-45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Transfer the granola to a large bowl.
Add the dried fruit (if using). Stir to combine.
Once cool, transfer to an air-tight container and store for up to 1 month.
Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion. Cook, stirring often, until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the garlic, thyme, black pepper, and salt. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the broth and barley.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the barley is tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the mixed vegetables and cooked chicken.
Cook until warmed through, about 4-6 minutes.
Serve warm.
Add the egg to a medium bowl and beat lightly.
Add the steak to the bowl with the egg and toss to coat.
Sprinkle the cornstarch over the steak and toss to coat.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together the orange juice, soy sauce, vinegar, and honey to make a sauce. Set aside.
Heat a large wok or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the scallions, garlic, and ginger. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds.
Add the steak to the pan and continue cooking, stirring often, until lightly browned, about 4-8 minutes.
Add the sauce and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer.
Add the stir-fry vegetables and cook until the vegetables are heated through, about 4-6 minutes.
Serve warm, on its own or over a cooked grain if desired.
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Evenly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Place one of the tortillas on the baking sheet.
Sprinkle ⅓ cup of the cheese over the tortilla, in an even layer.
Add the bell pepper, broccoli, chicken, tomato, onion, beans, and hot sauce.
Top with the remaining ⅓ cup cheese.
Place the second tortilla on top.
Place the baking sheet in the oven.
Cook until the tortillas are crisp and the cheese is melted, about 10-15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Cover a 9x13-inch baking sheet with foil and spray the foil with nonstick spray. Set aside.
Set up a breading station by placing three bowls, pie dishes, or other shallow dishes in a row.
In the first dish, add the flour. In the second dish, add the milk. In the third dish, add and stir together the breadcrumbs, parmesan, and seasoning blend.
Dip one strip of fish into the flour (first dish) to coat it evenly on all sides. Shake off any excess flour.
Add the strip of fish to the milk (second dish) to coat evenly on all sides. Shake to remove any excess milk.
Add the strip of fish to the breadcrumb mixture (third dish) to coat it evenly on all sides.
Place the strip of fish onto the prepared baking sheet.
Repeat steps 4-7 with the remaining strips of fish, then discard any leftover breading ingredients.
Bake the breaded fish strips for 10 minutes, then flip each strip over and continue baking until golden-brown and cooked through, about 5-10 minutes. Serve immediately.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Meanwhile, remove the outer leaves from the cauliflower head, then cut the florets away from the stalk. Discard the stalk and leaves.
Cut the cauliflower florets into bite-sized (about 1-inch) pieces.
Add the cauliflower, oil, salt, and black pepper to a large bowl. Toss to combine and coat the cauliflower.
Transfer the cauliflower to a baking sheet and spread into an even layer.
Bake until fork-tender and starting to brown, about 20-25 minutes, stirring about halfway through the cooking time.
Serve warm.
Using a spiralizer, cut the zucchini into noodles.
Heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the zucchini noodles and cook, tossing occasionally, until slightly wilted and tender, about 5 minutes. Be careful to not overcook or they will get mushy.
Remove from the heat.
Add the parmesan, black pepper, and basil. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Pasta Skillet with Sausage and Vegetables

steps.text: Cook the pasta according to the box directions. Before draining the pasta, measure off ½ cup of the pasta cooking water. Drain the pasta into a colander and set aside.
Place the empty pasta pot back on the stove over medium heat. Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the selected vegetables. Cook, stirring often, until tender, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook, stirring often, for 3-5 minutes.
Add the marinara sauce and Italian seasoning. Add the reserved pasta water, as needed, to thin out the sauce if it gets too thick and evaporated as you cook.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until simmering, about 4-5 minutes. Then add the cooked pasta and stir to combine.
Remove from heat and add the parmesan. Serve warm.
Add the bananas, milk, and peanut butter to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and thick (milkshake consistency), add more milk as needed to adjust the consistency.
Serve immediately.
Coat the inside of a 9x13-inch baking dish with nonstick spray.
In a large mixing bowl, stir together the flax meal, peanut butter, honey, and vanilla.
Add the oats, dried cherries and sliced almonds. Stir to combine.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared pan and press firmly into an even layer. Cover with a lid or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator to chill for at least 1 hour.
Remove from the refrigerator and cut into 24 bars, then serve or wrap each in plastic wrap and store in refrigerator for up to 14 days.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the pita bread rounds on the baking sheet and bake for 5 minutes
Remove from the oven and spread 2 tablespoons of the pesto on each pita round, leaving about a ½-inch area around the edges.
Top each pita round with ¼ cup of the bell pepper and ¼ cup of the chickpeas.
Sprinkle each pita round with 2 tablespoons of the mozzarella.
Place back in the oven and bake until the cheese has melted and the bell peppers are soft, about 9-11 minutes.
Serve warm.
Add the quinoa and water to a medium saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to a simmer.
Cover the saucepan with a lid and cook until the quinoa is tender and the water is absorbed, about 10-15 minutes. Remove the saucepan from the heat and set aside.
While the quinoa cooks, heat the oil and garlic in a medium skillet over medium heat just until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach. Cook, stirring often, until the spinach is wilted and the green beans are tender. Turn off the heat.
Add the cooked quinoa, tomatoes, beans, pesto, and pepper. Toss until well combined.
Divide into five serving bowls.
Serve warm, topping each bowl with 1 tablespoon parmesan cheese if desired.
In a medium mixing bowl, add the tomatoes, jalapeno or serrano chiles, cilantro, lime juice, onion, and salt.
Stir to combine.
Set in the refrigerator to chill for at least 15 minutes before serving.
Serve cold or at room temperature, as a dip or a condiment.
Peel the pears and cut them in half. Remove the cores with a spoon or melon baller.
Place the pears flat-side-down in a large saucepan.
Pour the pomegranate juice over the pears and add the cinnamon stick to the pan.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Cover the pan with a lid and reduce the heat to low.
Simmer gently until the pears are tender when pierced with a fork, about 25-30 minutes, turning them over gently once or twice while they cook so they color evenly.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the pears to a serving dish.
Garnish each pear half with 2 tablespoons of the yogurt and ½ tablespoon of the toasted almonds.
Serve warm.
In a microwave-safe bowl, stir together the oats, milk, hemp hearts, flax meal or chia seeds, maple syrup or brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt.
Microwave on high power (default setting) for 2 minutes.
Remove from the microwave and let sit to thicken and cool slightly, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve warm.
Add the cream cheese and Greek yogurt to the bowl of a food processor. Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the pumpkin puree, pumpkin pie spice, maple syrup or honey, and salt. Blend until completely combined, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a medium serving bowl or storage container.
Cover with a lid or plastic wrap. Place in the refrigerator to chill for at least 30 minutes.
Serve cold.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the milk and pudding mix for 2 minutes. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the pumpkin, cinnamon, ginger, and allspice.
Add the pumpkin mixture to the prepared pudding. Stir to combine.
Gently fold ½ cup of the whipped topping into the pumpkin-pudding mixture until combined.
Divide the mixture between four serving bowls.
Refrigerate until set, about 1 hour.
Serve cold, garnishing each serving with 2 tablespoons of the remaining whipped topping.
In a small to medium mixing bowl, whisk together the vinegar, oil, sugar or honey, salt, and black pepper.
Add the onion and toss to coat.
Let sit at room temperature for 1 hour or in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Serve as desired. Quick-pickled onions will keep in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
Add the quinoa to a small mixing bowl. Add enough water to cover the quinoa by at least 1 inch. Let sit overnight, or at least 6 hours.
When the quinoa is done soaking, preheat the oven to 425°F.

Line a 9-inch round cake pan with a cut circle of parchment paper. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil to the pan. Spread the oil around with your hands or a pastry brush until the pan is evenly coated. Set aside.
Drain and rinse the soaked quinoa under running water.
Add the quinoa and ¼ cup water to a blender or food processor.
Add the baking powder, salt, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Blend until smooth and creamy. The mixture will look like a thick pancake batter.
Pour the quinoa crust batter into the prepared cake pan and spread into an even layer, then bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven, flip the quinoa crust over in the pan, then return it to oven. Bake until the crust is browned and the edges are crispy, about 10-15 minutes.

Top the crust with the sauce, cheese, and any other toppings you would like. Continue baking until the cheese has melted and started to brown and any vegetable toppings are tender, about 12-15 minutes.
Let the pizza cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a cutting board and cut into eight slices. Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 350°F. Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish with cooking spray and set aside.
Add the quinoa and water to a small saucepan and bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer. Cook until tender, about 10-15 minutes, then remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, heat a medium skillet or sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the oil, bell pepper, and onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes
Add the chili powder, cumin, and garlic powder. Cook until fragrant, about 30-60 seconds, then remove from the heat.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the beans, corn, enchilada sauce, green chiles, and ¼ cup of the cheese. Stir in the cooked quinoa and the vegetable mixture.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish. Top with remaining ¾ cup of cheese.
Spray one side of a sheet of foil with cooking spray and place over the baking dish. Wrap around the edges to seal.
Bake for 20 minutes, then remove foil and continue baking until the cheese is melted and the edges are bubbling, about 10 minutes. Let cool for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with the cilantro, then cut into four pieces and serve warm with the lime wedges.

recipes.title: Quinoa, Shrimp, and Black Bean Casserole

steps.text: Heat a medium or large saucepan (pot) over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the onion and garlic.
Cook, stirring often, until the onion is lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the quinoa, broth, cumin, cayenne pepper, and black pepper.
Increase the heat to high and bring mixture to a boil.
Cover the pot with a lid and reduce the heat to simmer.
Cook until the quinoa is tender and most of the broth has been absorbed, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in the frozen corn, cooked shrimp, black beans and cilantro.
Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through.

recipes.title: Ranch Seasoning Mix (for Dip or Dressing)

steps.text: Whisk all the dry seasoning mix ingredients together until blended. If you want a more finely-ground seasoning mix, pulse the mixture in a food processor until it reaches your desired consistency.

Store the dry seasoning mix in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. Three (3) tablespoons of the mix is equal to one packet of store-bought ranch seasoning mix. Make Dip or Dressing
To make ranch dip, add 1 tablespoon of the prepared mix to ⅔ cup plain Greek yogurt. To make ranch dressing, add 1 tablespoon of the mix to ⅓ cup milk and ⅓ cup plain Greek yogurt. Stir well.
In a medium saucepan, whisk together the oil, flour, chili powder, oregano, cumin, onion powder, garlic powder, and salt.
Place the saucepan over medium heat. Heat until bubbling and fragrant, about 3-5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, and brown sugar. Whisk to combine.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer. Cook until slightly thickened, about 8-10 minutes.
Use in recipes as desired. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 14 days or in the freezer up to 6 months.
Add the tomatoes, garlic, oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, sugar, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using) to a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth, about 1-2 minutes.
Use right away, or keep in the refrigerator until needed.
Prepare rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add onions, carrots, and celery to skillet and sauté about 2- 4 minutes.
Add mushrooms to skillet and sauté about 4-5 minutes more.
Stir peas into vegetable mixture until warmed through.
Remove vegetable mixture from skillet and stir into prepared rice.
Add dried fruit to rice and vegetable mixture and mix well.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
On a baking sheet, toss the beets with 2 tablespoons of the oil, ¼ teaspoon of the salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the black pepper. Roast until tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat a large pot over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the carrots, onion, the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, and the remaining ¼ teaspoon black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, until beginning to soften, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme. Cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the broth and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to maintain a simmer.
Cook until the carrots are tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Transfer the beets to a blender, along with the carrots, onion, and enough broth to fill the blender about halfway.
Remove the plastic piece from the center of the blender lid and place a towel over the hole. Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes.
Return the pureed mixture to the pot and stir in the vinegar and sugar or honey. Reheat over the stovetop if needed.
In a small mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt and dill.
Serve warm or chill before serving, topping each serving with 1 tablespoon of the yogurt-dill mixture and 2 tablespoons of the chopped apple.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Place the beet pieces on a baking sheet and toss with ½ tablespoon of the oil. Place in the oven and roast until fork-tender, about 30-40 minutes.
Meanwhile add the garlic and 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice to a small bowl and stir to combine. Set aside.
Add ¼ cup of the roasted beet to a food processor. Pulse until broken down into small pieces.

Add the garlic-lemon juice mixture, ½ teaspoon lemon zest, beans, tahini, salt, and black pepper. Puree the mixture until very smooth, while slowly drizzling in the remaining 3½ tablespoons of oil, about 3-4 minutes.
Finely chop the remaining roasted beet. Add to a small bowl and toss with any remaining lemon zest and 1 tablespoon lemon juice. Set aside.
Transfer the pureed mixture to a serving dish and garnish with the chopped beet and lemon mixture.
Serve right away, or store in an air-tight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. May be frozen if desired.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a medium bowl, toss together the beets, oil, and salt.
Transfer the beets to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast for until fork tender, about 25-30 minutes, tossing halfway through the cooking time.
Remove from the oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 8-10 minutes.
Return the beets to the bowl.
Add the parsley, balsamic vinegar, and red wine vinegar. Toss to combine.
Serve right away, or chill before serving. Top each serving with 1 tablespoon of the feta just before serving.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set aside.
In a medium mixing bowl, stir together the yogurt, parsley, jalapeño, lemon juice, and black pepper. Set aside.
In a separate large mixing bowl, stir together the oil, garlic, coriander, cumin, paprika, and salt.
Add the broccoli, fennel, and chickpeas. Toss to combine and coat with the oil-seasoning mixture
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet, spreading it into a single layer.
Roast for 12 minutes, then remove from the oven and stir the mixture on the baking sheet.
Spread the mixture back out into a single layer, then place back in the oven.
Continue cooking until browned and the vegetables are fork-tender, about 10-12 minutes.
Transfer the roasted vegetable-chickpea mixture to the bowl with the yogurt mixture. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Prepare the Brussels sprouts by removing the outer leaves if dry or discolored, trimming the stems off, and cutting each sprout in half lengthwise.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, mustard, thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Add the Brussels sprouts and carrots. Toss to combine.
Transfer the Brussels sprouts and carrots to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast in the oven for 15 minutes, then remove from the oven and toss the Brussels sprouts and carrots on the baking sheet.
Spread the Brussels sprouts and carrots back into a single layer, then continue cooking in the oven until fork-tender, about 10-15 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat oven to 400°F.
In a medium mixing bowl, toss together the eggplant, onion, oil, salt, and black pepper.
Transfer the mixture to a baking sheet and spread into a single layer.
Roast in preheated oven until caramelized and tender, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove from oven and set aside to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.
Transfer the roasted vegetable mixture to a food processor or high-powered blender and add the tomato paste.
Pulse to chop up and mix in the tomato paste. The spread will remain chunky.
Serve right away.
Preheat oven to 450°F.
Remove the cores from the tomatoes. Cut about three-quarters of the tomatoes into wedges. Cut the tomatoes into a dice.
Peel the garlic cloves. Mince 1 clove, leaving the rest whole.
On a baking sheet, toss together the tomato wedges, onion, whole garlic cloves, oil, and salt.
Roast until the tomatoes are soft and spotty-brown, about 30-45 minutes. Set aside to cool slightly.
Meanwhile, in a medium mixing bowl, stir together the diced tomatoes, minced garlic, and basil. Set aside to marinate for 30 minutes.
Working in batches if needed, transfer the roasted vegetables to a food processor or high-powered blender and blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes.
Transfer the pureed mixture to a medium saucepan.
Add the marinated tomatoes and sugar or honey. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve warm.
Preheat oven broiler to high.
Line a baking sheet with a large piece of aluminum foil.
Place the jalapenos and onion on the baking sheet and toss with oil.
Place under the broiler, on the middle rack if your broiler is inside the oven and broil for 5 minutes.
Turn the jalapenos and onion pieces over, then add the garlic cloves to the baking sheet. Continue broiling until the vegetable are spotty-brown and charred in places, about 5 minutes.
Wrap the vegetables tightly with the foil and set aside for 20 minutes.
Open the foil carefully. One at a time, run the jalapenos under cool water while rubbing to remove the skins. Split the jalapenos lengthwise and scrape out the seeds.
Place the jalapenos, onion, garlic, lime juice, water, sugar, and salt in a blender. Blend until smooth, about 2 minutes.
Serve right away or chill before serving. Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 7 days.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Add the kohlrabi, beets, and fennel to a baking sheet.
Add the oil, salt, and black pepper. Toss to combine.
Roast in the oven until fork-tender, about 25-30 minutes, stirring about halfway through the cooking time.
Remove from oven.
Add the parmesan and parsley. Toss to combine.
Serve warm.
Move an oven rack to be about 10 inches from the broiler. Preheat the oven broiler to high.

Place the bell pepper and tomatoes on a baking sheet, skin-side-up. Place under the broiler until the skins are blistered and slightly blackened, about 10-15 minutes. Keep a close watch and rotate halfway through for even cooking.
Remove from the oven. Transfer the bell pepper and tomatoes to a heatproof bowl. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and set aside for 10-15 minutes.
Remove the skins from the bell pepper and tomatoes.
Add the bell pepper, tomatoes, oil, almonds, vinegar, parsley, garlic, paprika, salt, black pepper, and cayenne (if using) to a food processor or blender.
Blend until smooth, about 2-3 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed.
Serve right away, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Freeze for up to 3 months.
Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Line a baking sheet or casserole dish with parchment paper.
Place the selected vegetables in a large bowl.
Add the oil, garlic, black pepper, and salt. Toss to coat the vegetables.
Spread the vegetables out onto the prepared baking sheet or casserole dish in a single layer.
Bake until fork-tender, about 20-25 minutes, tossing about halfway through cooking for more even browning if desired.
(Optional) Top with the parmesan and parsley, and return to oven to broil until golden-brown, about 3-5 minutes, watching closely so they do not burn.
Serve warm.
Heat a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the chard stems, scallions, and garlic scapes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the stems are tender, about 6-8 minutes.
Add the chard leaves and water. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 3 minutes.
Remove the lid. Add the salt, black pepper, and nutmeg. Continue cooking uncovered for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and drizzle with balsamic vinegar. Serve warm.
Toast the slice of bread to your desired level of doneness.
Cut the egg and avocado into slices.
Layer the toast with the following ingredients, in this order: egg, avocado, and salsa.
Serve immediately.
Pre-heat the oven to 400°F.
Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper or coat with nonstick cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, toss the diced sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil and half of the salt and pepper.
Spread on prepared baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes.
Using the same bowl, add the chicken and fresh vegetables. Coat with 1 tablespoon oil and the remaining salt and pepper, lemon juice and zest, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder. Toss to coat.
Once the sweet potatoes have cooked for 10 minutes, add the chicken and vegetables to the pan with the potatoes. Toss and spread evenly.
Bake for 20 more minutes, tossing halfway through, until the chicken is cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Sprinkle with parmesan. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Veggie Bake

steps.text: Pre-heat the oven to 425°F.
Prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper or coat with nonstick cooking spray.
Spread the bell peppers and onions , or fresh vegetables, in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Add the slices of chicken sausage over the vegetables.
Add the diced butternut squash or sweet potato over the chicken sausage and vegetables.
